```{r}
ggarrange(p_cascade, p_access, p_paralog, nrow = 1, labels = "AUTO", widths = c(1.3, 1, 1))
```

### Clade identity

Clades were assigned in two independent ways. **Mitochondrial:** each individual's reads were mapped to one partial mitogenome per clade, and the clade was taken from the reads covering the COI barcode region. **Nuclear:** genome-wide genotype likelihoods (PCAngsd, NGSadmix) on all kept libraries. The two agree for every individual. Two libraries contained DNA from individuals of two different clades (both mitochondrial and nuclear signals mixed) and were excluded.

```{r}
#| label: mito-read-split
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 9
mito_long <- mito %>%
  select(sample_id, starts_with("coi_reads_mtDNA_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(-sample_id, names_to = "contig", values_to = "reads",
               names_prefix = "coi_reads_mtDNA_") %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  mutate(prop = reads / sum(reads)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  inner_join(select(seq_data, sample_id, site_code, season, replicate, tube), by = "sample_id") %>%
  mutate(contig = factor(contig, levels = tonsa_clades),
         ind = sprintf("%d_%02d", replicate, tube))

ggplot(mito_long, aes(x = ind, y = prop, fill = contig)) +
  facet_grid(site_code ~ season) +
  geom_col(width = 1, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = clade_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Individual (assay_tube)", y = "Share of COI reads", fill = "Mito contig") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 290, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, size = 7))
```

All four clades are cleanly separated in the nuclear genome. Clade F splits further into site-specific sub-lineages (Manatee River, Ft. Hamer, and the Chesapeake/New England group), visible on PC4 and at K = 5–6.

```{r}
#| label: clade-structure
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 10
pca_full <- read_cx("results", "04_structure", "all", "pcangsd_scores.tsv")
cov_all <- as.matrix(read.table(cx("results", "04_structure", "all", "pcangsd.cov")))
ve <- eigen(cov_all, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
ve <- round(100 * ve / sum(ve), 1)

# PCAngsd / NGSadmix were run on all kept libraries; the two mixed (unassigned)
# libraries are dropped from the plots only
pca_full <- pca_full %>%
  left_join(select(clades, sample_id, clade, lineage), by = "sample_id")
pca_all <- pca_full %>%
  filter(clade %in% tonsa_clades) %>%
  mutate(clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades))

pca_plot <- function(a, b) {
  ggplot(pca_all, aes(x = .data[[a]], y = .data[[b]], colour = clade, shape = clade)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.85) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = clade_cols[tonsa_clades]) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = clade_shapes[tonsa_clades]) +
    labs(x = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", a, ve[as.integer(sub("PC", "", a))]),
         y = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", b, ve[as.integer(sub("PC", "", b))]),
         colour = "Clade", shape = "Clade") +
    theme_matt(base_size = 13)
}

# NGSadmix: best of 3 runs per K; clusters coloured by the clade that dominates them
best_run <- function(K) {
  likes <- sapply(1:3, function(r) {
    l <- readLines(cx("results", "04_structure", "all", "ngsadmix", sprintf("K%d_rep%d.log", K, r)))
    as.numeric(sub(".*best like=([-0-9.e]+).*", "\\1", grep("best like", l, value = TRUE)[1]))
  })
  which.max(likes)
}
ord <- pca_all %>%
  mutate(lin = factor(lineage, levels = c("X", "S", "IV", "F-N", "F-NE", "F-FH", "F-MR")),
         site_code = factor(site, levels = site_order)) %>%
  arrange(lin, site_code, sampling_event) %>% pull(sample_id)
f_shades <- c(clade_cols[["F"]], "#F36E6D", "#7C2B2B", "#FFB3B2")   # F plus lighter / darker shades
admix <- map_dfr(3:6, function(K) {
  q <- read.table(cx("results", "04_structure", "all", "ngsadmix", sprintf("K%d_rep%d.qopt", K, best_run(K))))
  q$sample_id <- pca_full$sample_id   # rows follow the full analysis set
  long <- pivot_longer(q, -sample_id, names_to = "cluster", values_to = "q") %>%
    filter(sample_id %in% pca_all$sample_id)
  dom <- long %>% group_by(sample_id) %>% slice_max(q, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
    left_join(select(pca_all, sample_id, clade), by = "sample_id") %>%
    count(cluster, clade) %>% group_by(cluster) %>% slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  long %>% left_join(select(dom, cluster, top = clade), by = "cluster") %>% mutate(K = paste0("K = ", K))
}) %>%
  mutate(sample_id = factor(sample_id, levels = ord))
fill_map <- admix %>% distinct(K, cluster, top) %>% group_by(K, top) %>%
  mutate(col = if_else(top == "F", f_shades[row_number()], clade_cols[as.character(top)])) %>%
  ungroup() %>% mutate(key = paste(K, cluster))
admix <- admix %>% mutate(key = paste(K, cluster))

p_admix <- ggplot(admix, aes(x = sample_id, y = q, fill = key)) +
  facet_grid(K ~ .) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(fill_map$col, fill_map$key), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Individuals, grouped by lineage (X, S, IV, F-N, F-NE, F-FH, F-MR) and site", y = "Ancestry") +
  theme_matt_facets(base_size = 13) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

ggarrange(ggarrange(pca_plot("PC1", "PC2"), pca_plot("PC3", "PC4"), nrow = 1,
                    common.legend = TRUE, legend = "right", labels = c("A", "B")),
          p_admix, nrow = 2, heights = c(1, 1.1), labels = c("", "C"))
```

Within clade F, the sub-lineages are clearly separated (2–6% COI divergence) but much less divergent than the clades are from each other (12–18%). We therefore analyse four clades, and keep the F sub-lineage as an annotation.

```{r}
#| label: coi-divergence
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
fa <- readLines(cx("results", "03_clades", "mito", "coi_aligned.fa"))
hdr <- grepl("^>", fa)
seq_id <- sub("^>(\\S+).*", "\\1", fa[hdr])
seqs <- tapply(fa[!hdr], cumsum(hdr)[!hdr], paste, collapse = "")
names(seqs) <- seq_id
lin <- clades %>% filter(clade %in% tonsa_clades, sample_id %in% seq_id) %>%
  mutate(group = if_else(clade == "F", lineage, clade))
mat <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(toupper(seqs[lin$sample_id]), ""))
ok <- matrix(mat %in% c("A", "C", "G", "T"), nrow = nrow(mat))
n <- nrow(mat); diff <- matrix(0, n, n); comp <- matrix(0, n, n)
for (j in seq_len(ncol(mat))) {
  v <- ok[, j]
  both <- outer(v, v, "&")
  comp <- comp + both
  diff <- diff + (outer(mat[, j], mat[, j], "!=") & both)
}
pd <- diff / comp
grp <- lin$group
grp_levels <- intersect(c("X", "S", "IV", "F-N", "F-NE", "F-FH", "F-MR"), unique(grp))
div <- expand_grid(a = grp_levels, b = grp_levels) %>%
  mutate(pdist = map2_dbl(a, b, function(x, y) {
    m <- pd[grp == x, grp == y, drop = FALSE]
    if (x == y) mean(m[upper.tri(m)]) else mean(m)
  }) * 100,
  a = factor(a, levels = grp_levels), b = factor(b, levels = rev(grp_levels)))

ggplot(div, aes(x = a, y = b, fill = pdist)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", pdist), colour = pdist > 9), size = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "white", "FALSE" = "grey15"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F2F2F0", high = "#2B2B29", name = "COI\ndistance (%)") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_matt(base_size = 13) +
  theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())
```

#### Lineage phylogeny: mitochondrial vs nuclear

Mitochondrial relationships come from the COI maximum-likelihood tree (IQ-TREE, all individuals and reference haplotypes), reduced to one representative per lineage (the individual with the most complete COI sequence) and rooted on *A. hudsonica*. Support values are ultrafast bootstraps of the corresponding node in the full tree. Nuclear relationships come from genome-wide individual covariances (PCAngsd, all individuals): pairwise distances d~ij~ = C~ii~ + C~jj~ − 2C~ij~ were averaged between lineages and corrected for within-lineage distance (net distance), and a neighbour-joining tree was built from them (midpoint-rooted; support = percentage of 200 bootstrap replicates resampling individuals within lineages).

```{r}
#| label: lineage-phylogeny
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5
lin_levels <- c("X", "S", "IV", "F-N", "F-NE", "F-FH", "F-MR")
lin_col <- c(X = clade_cols[["X"]], S = clade_cols[["S"]], IV = clade_cols[["IV"]],
             `F-N` = f_shades[1], `F-NE` = f_shades[2], `F-FH` = f_shades[3], `F-MR` = f_shades[4])
lin_n <- clades %>% filter(lineage %in% lin_levels) %>% count(lineage)

# mitochondrial: COI tree reduced to one tip per lineage plus outgroups
coi_tr <- ape::read.tree(cx("results", "03_clades", "mito", "coi_tree.contree"))
coi_miss <- read_cx("results", "03_clades", "mito", "coi_missingness.tsv")
reps <- coi_miss %>%
  filter(included == "yes", flag == "ok", sample_id %in% coi_tr$tip.label) %>%
  inner_join(select(clades, sample_id, lineage), by = "sample_id") %>%
  filter(lineage %in% lin_levels) %>%
  group_by(lineage) %>% slice_min(frac_missing, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()
outg <- c(A_hudsonica = grep("A_hudsonica", coi_tr$tip.label, value = TRUE)[1],
          A_lilljeborgi = grep("A_lilljeborgi", coi_tr$tip.label, value = TRUE)[1])
hud <- grep("A_hudsonica", coi_tr$tip.label, value = TRUE)
coi_full <- ape::root(coi_tr, outgroup = hud, resolve.root = TRUE)
coi_red <- ape::keep.tip(coi_full, c(reps$sample_id, outg))
# support: label of the matching node (same descendant tips' MRCA) in the full tree
full_sup <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(coi_full$node.label))
coi_red$node.label <- map_chr(seq_len(coi_red$Nnode) + ape::Ntip(coi_red), function(nd) {
  tips <- coi_red$tip.label[phangorn::Descendants(coi_red, nd, "tips")[[1]]]
  if (length(tips) == ape::Ntip(coi_red)) return("")
  m <- ape::getMRCA(coi_full, tips)
  v <- full_sup[m - ape::Ntip(coi_full)]
  if (is.na(v)) "" else as.character(round(v))
})
lab_of <- c(set_names(reps$lineage, reps$sample_id), set_names(c("A. hudsonica", "A. lilljeborgi"), outg))
coi_red$tip.label <- unname(lab_of[coi_red$tip.label])
coi_red <- ape::ladderize(coi_red)

# nuclear: net distances between lineages from the PCAngsd covariance
pc_ids <- read_cx("results", "04_structure", "all", "pcangsd_scores.tsv")$sample_id
Cm <- as.matrix(read.table(cx("results", "04_structure", "all", "pcangsd.cov")))
dimnames(Cm) <- list(pc_ids, pc_ids)
nuc_ind <- clades %>% filter(sample_id %in% pc_ids, lineage %in% lin_levels)
Dind <- outer(diag(Cm), diag(Cm), "+") - 2 * Cm
net_dist <- function(ids_by_lin) {
  L <- names(ids_by_lin)
  w <- map_dbl(ids_by_lin, function(i) { m <- Dind[i, i]; mean(m[upper.tri(m)]) })
  D <- outer(L, L, Vectorize(function(a, b)
    if (a == b) 0 else mean(Dind[ids_by_lin[[a]], ids_by_lin[[b]]]) - (w[[a]] + w[[b]]) / 2))
  dimnames(D) <- list(L, L)
  D
}
by_lin <- split(nuc_ind$sample_id, factor(nuc_ind$lineage, levels = lin_levels))
nuc_tr <- phangorn::midpoint(ape::nj(net_dist(by_lin)))
set.seed(1)
boots <- map(1:200, function(b) {
  bl <- map(by_lin, ~ sample(.x, length(.x), replace = TRUE))
  phangorn::midpoint(ape::nj(net_dist(bl)))
})
nuc_tr$node.label <- round(100 * ape::prop.clades(nuc_tr, boots) / length(boots))
nuc_tr$node.label[1] <- ""
nuc_tr <- ape::ladderize(nuc_tr)

tip_cols <- function(tr) unname(c(lin_col, `A. hudsonica` = "grey40", `A. lilljeborgi` = "grey40")[tr$tip.label])
tip_lab <- function(tr) {
  n <- lin_n$n[match(tr$tip.label, lin_n$lineage)]
  ifelse(is.na(n), tr$tip.label, sprintf("%s (n = %d)", tr$tip.label, n))
}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(3, 1, 3, 1))
for (k in 1:2) {
  tr <- if (k == 1) coi_red else nuc_tr
  tr2 <- tr; tr2$tip.label <- tip_lab(tr)
  ape::plot.phylo(tr2, tip.color = tip_cols(tr), font = ifelse(grepl("^A\\.", tr$tip.label), 3, 2),
                  cex = 1.1, label.offset = 0.002 * (k == 1) + 0.00002 * (k == 2), edge.width = 2,
                  x.lim = c(0, max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(tr)) * 1.6),
                  main = c("Mitochondrial (COI, ML)", "Nuclear (genome-wide, NJ)")[k])
  ape::nodelabels(tr$node.label, frame = "none", adj = c(1.2, -0.4), cex = 0.85)
  ape::add.scale.bar(cex = 0.8)
}
par(op)
```

The two genomes give the same tree. Unrooted, both split the clades into {S, IV} and {X, F}, with X sister to F (support 98 in COI, 100 in the nuclear tree), and both order the F lineages the same way: F-MR first, then F-FH, then F-N with F-NE. They differ only in where the root falls, and the nuclear root is a midpoint placement, not an estimate. Mito-nuclear concordance at every level means the lineages are not mitochondrial types introgressed onto a shared nuclear background: they are separate, non-interbreeding (or rarely interbreeding) genetic units. Nuclear distances from the PCAngsd covariance summarise genome-wide divergence rather than coming from a substitution model, so branch lengths in the two panels are not comparable.


```{r}
#| label: clade-props
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 9
seq_data %>%
  filter(clade %in% tonsa_clades) %>%
  mutate(clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades)) %>%
  droplevels() %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = season, fill = clade)) +
  facet_wrap(site_code ~ ., ncol = 2) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = clade_cols) +
  labs(x = "Season", y = "Count", fill = "Clade") +
  theme_matt_facets(base_size = 18)
```

#### Seasonal turnover of lineages

Lineage composition is compared among the collections at each site (sequenced individuals only; unassigned libraries excluded). Each site gets a Fisher exact test of lineage × season (simulated p, 10⁴ replicates). The combined test uses the sum of per-site χ² statistics, with season labels shuffled among individuals within each site (10⁴ permutations); sites with a single lineage contribute nothing.

```{r}
#| label: lineage-turnover
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5
season_levels <- c("early", "peak", "late")
lin_levels <- c("X", "S", "IV", "F-N", "F-NE", "F-FH", "F-MR")
lin_col <- c(X = clade_cols[["X"]], S = clade_cols[["S"]], IV = clade_cols[["IV"]],
             `F-N` = f_shades[1], `F-NE` = f_shades[2], `F-FH` = f_shades[3], `F-MR` = f_shades[4])
comp <- seq_data %>%
  filter(lineage %in% lin_levels, !sample_id %in% c("MR_peak_2_04", "MR_peak_2_05")) %>%
  mutate(season = factor(season, levels = season_levels),
         lineage = factor(lineage, levels = lin_levels),
         site_code = factor(site_code, levels = site_order))
coll_temp <- comp %>% group_by(site_code, season) %>%
  summarise(temp = mean(collection_temp, na.rm = TRUE), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

chi_stat <- function(lin, sea) {
  tb <- table(droplevels(lin), droplevels(sea))
  if (nrow(tb) < 2 || ncol(tb) < 2) return(0)
  suppressWarnings(unname(chisq.test(tb, correct = FALSE)$statistic))
}
set.seed(1)
turn_site <- comp %>% group_by(site_code) %>%
  summarise(seasons = n_distinct(season), lineages = n_distinct(lineage), individuals = n(),
            p = if (n_distinct(season) > 1 && n_distinct(lineage) > 1)
              fisher.test(table(droplevels(lineage), droplevels(season)), simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 1e4)$p.value
            else NA_real_,
            .groups = "drop")
obs_chi <- comp %>% group_by(site_code) %>% summarise(x = chi_stat(lineage, season)) %>% pull(x) %>% sum()
by_site <- split(comp, comp$site_code, drop = TRUE)
perm_chi <- replicate(1e4, sum(map_dbl(by_site, ~ chi_stat(.x$lineage, sample(.x$season)))))
turn_p <- (sum(perm_chi >= obs_chi) + 1) / (length(perm_chi) + 1)

ggplot(comp, aes(x = season, fill = lineage)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = coll_temp, aes(x = season, y = 1.06, label = sprintf("%.0f°C", temp)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.2) +
  geom_text(data = coll_temp, aes(x = season, y = -0.06, label = paste0("n=", n)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ site_code, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = lin_col, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), limits = c(-0.1, 1.1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion of sequenced individuals", fill = "Lineage",
       caption = "Labels: collection temperature (top) and individuals sequenced (bottom).") +
  theme_matt_facets(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: lineage-turnover-table
turn_site %>%
  left_join(comp %>% group_by(site_code, season) %>% count(lineage) %>%
              summarise(comp = paste(sprintf("%s %d", lineage, n), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") %>%
              group_by(site_code) %>%
              summarise(composition = paste(sprintf("%s: %s", season, comp), collapse = "; ")),
            by = "site_code") %>%
  transmute(Site = site_code, Seasons = seasons, Lineages = lineages, Individuals = individuals,
            `Fisher p` = if_else(is.na(p), "–", format.pval(p, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4)),
            Composition = composition) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf("Lineage composition by season at each site. Combined test across sites: χ² = %.0f, permutation p %s.",
                                 obs_chi, format.pval(turn_p, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4)))
```


### Genetic differentiation within clades

Population structure and diversity are analysed within each clade (X, F, S, IV), with populations defined as clade × site × sampling event (n ≥ 8). Within clade F, site differences include differences between F sub-lineages.

```{r}
#| label: within-clade-pca
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 9
wpca <- map_dfr(tonsa_clades, function(cl) {
  f <- cx("results", "04_structure", cl, "pcangsd_scores.tsv")
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  cv <- as.matrix(read.table(cx("results", "04_structure", cl, "pcangsd.cov")))
  v <- eigen(cv, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    transmute(sample_id, PC1, PC2, site, season = sampling_event,
              panel = sprintf("%s (n = %d): PC1 %.1f%%, PC2 %.1f%%", cl, n(), 100 * v[1] / sum(v), 100 * v[2] / sum(v)))
})
if (nrow(wpca) == 0) {
  cat("Within-clade PCAs are not in this export yet.")
} else {
  wpca %>%
    mutate(site = factor(site, levels = site_order),
           season = factor(season, levels = season_order),
           panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel))) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, fill = site, shape = season)) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free") +
    geom_point(size = 2.5, colour = "grey15", stroke = 0.3) +
    # 95% ellipse per site (t distribution, so a few outlying individuals don't
    # inflate it); sites with fewer than 4 individuals in a clade get no ellipse
    # stat_ellipse(data = ~ add_count(.x, panel, site) %>% filter(n >= 4),
    #              aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = site, group = site), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    #              type = "t", level = 0.95, linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pop_cols[site_order], guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pop_cols[site_order], drop = FALSE) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(early = 21, peak = 24, late = 22)) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21))) +
    labs(fill = "Site", shape = "Season") +
    theme_matt_facets(base_size = 13)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fst-pairs
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
fst_files <- Sys.glob(cx("results", "05_diversity", "fst", "*.fst.global.txt"))
if (length(fst_files) == 0) {
  cat("FST results are not in this export yet.")
} else {
  fst <- map_dfr(fst_files, function(f) {
    vals <- as.numeric(regmatches(readLines(f, warn = FALSE), gregexpr("-?[0-9.]+(e-?[0-9]+)?", readLines(f, warn = FALSE)))[[1]])
    pops <- strsplit(sub("\\.fst\\.global\\.txt$", "", basename(f)), ".vs.", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    tibble(pop1 = pops[1], pop2 = pops[2], fst_unweighted = tail(vals, 2)[1], fst_weighted = tail(vals, 1))
  }) %>%
    separate(pop1, c("clade", "site1", "season1"), sep = "__") %>%
    separate(pop2, c("clade2", "site2", "season2"), sep = "__") %>%
    filter(clade %in% tonsa_clades) %>%
    mutate(comparison = case_when(site1 == site2 ~ "seasonal (same site)",
                                  season1 == season2 ~ "spatial (same season)",
                                  TRUE ~ "site and season differ"),
           clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades))
  write_csv(fst, here("Output", "Output_data", "fst_pairs.csv"))
  ggplot(fst, aes(x = comparison, y = fst_weighted, fill = clade)) +
    geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) + 
    geom_point(size = 2.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = clade_cols) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = expression(F[ST]~"(weighted)")) +
    theme_matt_facets(base_size = 13) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
}
```

#### Isolation by distance

Genetic differentiation between sites within each clade, against the straight-line distance between sites. F<sub>ST</sub> is averaged over the season pairs available for each pair of sites. F pairs between sub-lineages (F-MR, F-FH, F-N) are shown separately: they reflect divergence between lineages, not gene flow between populations. Straight-line distances underestimate the distance by sea (around Florida, and around Nova Scotia between Maine and the Gulf of St. Lawrence), and each clade has only 2–4 sites, so this is descriptive.

```{r}
#| label: ibd
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
if (exists("fst") && nrow(fst) > 0) {
  haversine_km <- function(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) {
    rad <- pi / 180
    a <- sin((lat2 - lat1) * rad / 2)^2 + cos(lat1 * rad) * cos(lat2 * rad) * sin((lon2 - lon1) * rad / 2)^2
    2 * 6371 * asin(sqrt(a))
  }
  f_lineage <- c(MR = "F-MR", FH = "F-FH", MD = "F-N", GW = "F-N")
  coords <- site_data %>% distinct(site_code, lat, long)
  ibd <- fst %>%
    filter(site1 != site2) %>%
    mutate(a = pmin(site1, site2), b = pmax(site1, site2)) %>%
    group_by(clade, a, b) %>%
    summarise(fst = mean(fst_weighted), n_pairs = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    left_join(rename(coords, a = site_code, lat_a = lat, long_a = long), by = "a") %>%
    left_join(rename(coords, b = site_code, lat_b = lat, long_b = long), by = "b") %>%
    mutate(dist_km = haversine_km(lat_a, long_a, lat_b, long_b),
           fst_lin = fst / (1 - fst),
           comparison = if_else(clade == "F" & f_lineage[a] != f_lineage[b],
                                "between F sub-lineages", "within clade / sub-lineage"),
           label = paste(a, b, sep = "–"))
  write_csv(ibd, here("Output", "Output_data", "isolation_by_distance.csv"))
  ggplot(ibd, aes(x = dist_km, y = fst_lin, colour = clade, shape = comparison)) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 3, vjust = -0.9, check_overlap = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = clade_cols[tonsa_clades]) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("within clade / sub-lineage" = 16, "between F sub-lineages" = 1)) +
    labs(x = "Straight-line distance between sites (km, log scale)", y = expression(F[ST] / (1 - F[ST])),
         colour = "Clade", shape = NULL) +
    theme_matt(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "right")
} else {
  cat("FST results are not in this export yet.")
}
```

Shown below are estimates of diversity across the data set. Tajima's D can be used to detect random vs. non-random evolutionary processes (e.g. drift vs. selection). A value near zero indicates neutral processes and a stable population size. Negative values indicate an excess of rare alleles, suggesting possible recent selective sweeps or population expansion after a bottleneck. Positive values indicate possible population contraction or balancing selection, resulting in fewer rare alleles than expected.

Most values of Tajima's D for our data set are small (within 0.5 of 0). A few samples reached moderate values around -1 and 1. Interestingly, all cases are from the two sites in the Chesapeake, with a low Tajima's D value for S clade individuals at the high salinity site, and high values for F clade individuals at both high and low salinity sites.

We also calculated nucleotide diversity, which represents the average number of nucleotide differences between randomly sampled sequences in a population. Theta values tended to be high, with the exception of F Clade individuals at the low salinity site in Florida and the two sites in the Chesapeake.

We note that these diversity metrics should only be compared within clades since reference bias changes which sites are usable in each clade.

Within sites, there is notably little change in these metrics across seasons. Three general within-clade patterns can be seen across sites:

1.  **Increasing Tajima's D and decreased nucleotide diversity,** as seen in Clade F. This may indicate serial founder effects. Diversity should fall steadily in the direction of expansion ([Excoffier et al. 2009](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.ecolsys.39.110707.173414)). For a clade spreading north since the last glacial maximum, northern sites would be expected to have lower θπ and higher D ([Hewitt 2000](https://doi.org/10.1038/35016000)). This suggests a low latitude origin for this clade.
2.  **Consistently low Tajima's D and consistently high nucleotide diversity**, as seen in Clades S and IV (although note the limited sampling for these clades). This pattern suggests large, well-connected populations. There may have been population expansion before sites diverged, or there may be substantial gene flow between populations keeping them similar ([Excoffier et al. 2009](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.ecolsys.39.110707.173414)).
3.  **Consistently small Tajima's D and consistently high nucleotide diversity**, as seen in Clade X. While this typically would indicate large, stable populations, Clade X is found only at the high latitude sites, where populations of *Acartia tonsa* are present during only part of the year, exhibiting drastic fluctuations in population size over this period. This may indicate the importance of an egg bank / resting eggs. If the population is generated each year by hatching out of eggs laid over many previous years, diversity would remain high. The egg bank acts as a store of diversity, so a brief active season doesn’t mean a small genetic population ([Hairston 1996](https://doi.org/10.4319/lo.1996.41.5.1087)). Resting eggs are well documented in *Acartia* (Marcus 1996, *Hydrobiologia* 320:141–152). In Narragansett Bay, *A. tonsa* replaces the egg-banking *A. hudsonica* each summer ([Sullivan & McManus 1986](https://doi.org/10.3354/meps028121)), the same seasonal turnover your ME site shows. Under these dynamics, individual sites may retain distinct populations, as seen in the within-clade PCAs above.

```{r}
#| label: diversity-pops
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
# Genome-wide theta_W, theta_pi and Tajima's D per population, with 95% CIs.
# Preferred: block bootstrap over 1 Mb blocks (diversity_ci.tsv, rule tajima_boot).
# Fallback for older exports: delete-one-chromosome jackknife (15 blocks, crude)
# from the per-chromosome thetaStat output. D is always computed from summed
# thetas, not by averaging per-block D.
tajima_D <- function(tw, tp, n_ind) {
  nchr <- 2 * n_ind
  i <- seq_len(nchr - 1)
  a1 <- sum(1 / i); a2 <- sum(1 / i^2)
  b1 <- (nchr + 1) / (3 * (nchr - 1)); b2 <- 2 * (nchr^2 + nchr + 3) / (9 * nchr * (nchr - 1))
  c1 <- b1 - 1 / a1; c2 <- b2 - (nchr + 2) / (a1 * nchr) + a2 / a1^2
  e1 <- c1 / a1; e2 <- c2 / (a1^2 + a2)
  S <- tw * a1
  (tp - tw) / sqrt(e1 * S + e2 * S * (S - 1))
}
jackknife_pop <- function(pop, n_ind) {
  f <- cx("results", "05_diversity", "thetas", paste0(pop, ".thetas.idx.pestPG"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  t <- read.table(f, comment.char = "", skip = 1)
  tw <- t[[4]]; tp <- t[[5]]; ns <- t[[14]]; g <- length(ns)
  est <- function(keep) c(tajima_D(sum(tw[keep]), sum(tp[keep]), n_ind),
                          sum(tp[keep]) / sum(ns[keep]), sum(tw[keep]) / sum(ns[keep]))
  full <- est(rep(TRUE, g))
  loo <- sapply(seq_len(g), function(j) est(seq_len(g) != j))
  se <- sqrt((g - 1) / g * rowSums((loo - rowMeans(loo))^2))
  tibble(population = pop, n_ind = n_ind, n_sites = sum(ns),
         tajima_D = full[1], tajima_D_lo95 = full[1] - 1.96 * se[1], tajima_D_hi95 = full[1] + 1.96 * se[1],
         pi = full[2], pi_lo95 = full[2] - 1.96 * se[2], pi_hi95 = full[2] + 1.96 * se[2],
         theta_W = full[3], ci_method = "chromosome jackknife (15 blocks)")
}

ci_file  <- cx("results", "05_diversity", "diversity_ci.tsv")
pop_file <- cx("results", "05_diversity", "populations.tsv")
if (file.exists(ci_file)) {
  div_pop <- read_tsv(ci_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(ci_method = "block bootstrap (1 Mb blocks)")
} else if (file.exists(pop_file)) {
  pops <- read_tsv(pop_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  div_pop <- map2_dfr(pops$population, pops$n, jackknife_pop)
} else {
  div_pop <- tibble()
}

if (nrow(div_pop) == 0) {
  cat("Diversity estimates are not in this export yet.")
} else {
  div_pop <- div_pop %>%
    separate(population, c("clade", "site", "season"), sep = "__", remove = FALSE) %>%
    filter(clade %in% tonsa_clades) %>%
    mutate(clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades),
           site = factor(site, levels = site_order),
           season = factor(season, levels = season_order))
  write_csv(div_pop, here("Output", "Output_data", "diversity_populations.csv"))
  div_pop %>%
    transmute(clade, site, season,
              `θπ per site_est` = pi, `θπ per site_lo` = pi_lo95, `θπ per site_hi` = pi_hi95,
              `Tajima's D_est` = tajima_D, `Tajima's D_lo` = tajima_D_lo95, `Tajima's D_hi` = tajima_D_hi95) %>%
    pivot_longer(-c(clade, site, season), names_to = c("stat", ".value"), names_sep = "_(?=[^_]+$)") %>%
    mutate(stat = factor(stat, levels = c("θπ per site", "Tajima's D"))) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = site, y = est, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, shape = season, colour = clade)) +
    facet_grid(stat ~ clade, scales = "free", space = "free_x") +
    geom_hline(data = tibble(stat = factor("Tajima's D", levels = c("θπ per site", "Tajima's D")), y = 0), aes(yintercept = y),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey70", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_pointrange(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 1, fatten = 2.5) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = clade_cols, guide = "none") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(early = 16, peak = 17, late = 15)) +
    labs(x = "Site (south → north)", y = NULL, shape = "Season",
         caption = paste("Bars: 95% CI,", unique(div_pop$ci_method))) +
    theme_matt_facets(base_size = 13)
}
```

Diversity is compared within clades only: reference bias changes which sites are usable in each clade. The spectra are folded (no outgroup), and low-coverage data shift the absolute values of Tajima's D, so differences between populations of the same clade are more informative than whether D is above or below zero. Confidence intervals come from a block bootstrap over 1 Mb blocks; populations of 8 individuals (F MD late, S MR late) are the least precise.
### Linkage disequilibrium

LD was estimated with ngsLD within each clade on every fifth SNP (MAF ≥ 0.05), for a random 2% of SNP pairs up to 100 kb apart, and averaged in distance bins. Dashed lines show the r² expected between unlinked SNPs from sample size alone (≈ 1/n). LD decays to near that level within a few kb in X, S and IV, as expected for very large long-term population sizes. The higher plateau in F reflects allele-frequency differences between the F sub-lineages pooled in the clade, not physical linkage.

```{r}
#| label: ld-decay
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
ld_files <- Sys.glob(cx("results", "07_ld", "*.ld_decay.tsv"))
if (length(ld_files) == 0) {
  cat("LD decay is not in this export yet.")
} else {
  ld <- map_dfr(ld_files, ~ read_tsv(.x, col_types = cols(clade = "c"))) %>%   # "F" would otherwise be read as FALSE
    filter(n_pairs >= 50) %>%                 # drop sparse edge bins
    mutate(width = case_when(bin_start_bp < 1000 ~ 100, bin_start_bp < 10000 ~ 1000, TRUE ~ 5000),
           mid_kb = (bin_start_bp + width / 2) / 1000,
           clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades))
  n_clade <- seq_data %>% filter(clade %in% tonsa_clades, !library_failed) %>%
    count(clade) %>% mutate(clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades), r2_null = 1 / n)
  write_csv(ld, here("Output", "Output_data", "ld_decay.csv"))
  ggplot(ld, aes(x = mid_kb, y = mean_r2_ExpG, colour = clade)) +
    geom_hline(data = n_clade, aes(yintercept = r2_null, colour = clade), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(size = 1.2) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100), labels = c("0.1", "0.3", "1", "3", "10", "30", "100")) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = clade_cols[tonsa_clades]) +
    labs(x = "Distance between SNPs (kb, log scale)", y = expression(Mean~italic(r)^2), colour = "Clade") +
    theme_matt(base_size = 14)
}
```

### Relatedness and sample quality

Relatedness was estimated with ngsRelate for every pair of individuals within each population. KING-robust kinship does not depend on allele frequencies, so it is less affected than *r*<sub>ab</sub> by the small samples per population: unrelated pairs fall near or below 0, second-degree relatives near 0.125 and first-degree relatives near 0.25. In panel B, related pairs move towards high R1 and high KING; pairs above 0.1 are labelled.

```{r}
#| label: relatedness
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 6
rel_file <- cx("results", "06_relatedness", "relatedness.tsv")
if (!file.exists(rel_file)) {
  cat("Relatedness is not in this export yet.")
} else {
  rel <- read_tsv(rel_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    select(population, ida, idb, nSites, rab, KING, R0, R1) %>%
    separate(population, c("clade", "site", "season"), sep = "__", remove = FALSE) %>%
    filter(clade %in% tonsa_clades) %>%
    mutate(clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades),
           site = factor(site, levels = site_order),
           season = factor(season, levels = season_order),
           flag = KING > 0.1,
           pair = paste(ida, idb, sep = " × "))
  rel <- rel %>% mutate(collection = factor(paste(site, season),
                                            levels = unique(paste(site, season)[order(site, season)])))
  write_csv(rel, here("Output", "Output_data", "relatedness_pairs.csv"))
  # x labels carry the median number of sites per pair (precision of the estimates)
  site_n <- rel %>% group_by(collection) %>%
    summarise(lab = sprintf("%s\n(%.1fk sites)", first(collection), median(nSites) / 1000), .groups = "drop")
  rel <- rel %>% mutate(collection = factor(collection, levels = site_n$collection, labels = site_n$lab))

  p_king <- ggplot(rel, aes(x = collection, y = KING)) +
    facet_grid(~ clade, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.125, 0.25), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
    geom_jitter(aes(colour = flag), width = 0.2, height = 0, size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey55", `TRUE` = "#B73534"), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "KING-robust kinship") +
    theme_matt_facets(base_size = 12) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 8))

  p_r1 <- ggplot(rel, aes(x = KING, y = R1)) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = clade), size = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = filter(rel, flag), shape = 21, size = 3, colour = "black") +
    geom_text(data = filter(rel, flag), aes(label = pair), hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = clade_cols[tonsa_clades]) +
    labs(x = "KING-robust kinship", y = "R1", colour = "Clade") +
    theme_matt(base_size = 12)

  ggarrange(p_king, p_r1, nrow = 1, widths = c(1.7, 1), labels = "AUTO")
}
```

In MR peak, MR_peak_1_09 belongs to the F-FH sub-lineage while the rest are F-MR, so its kinship with every other individual is strongly negative (the cluster near −1.1). MR_peak_2_04 and MR_peak_2_05 carry about 15% and 22% F-N ancestry (NGSadmix, K = 6) and have elevated kinship with each other (KING 0.20, R0 0.11). The heterozygosity check below shows both are far more heterozygous than any other F individual (F = −0.18 and −0.22; clade median 0.13), so their libraries most likely contain DNA from a second individual rather than coming from admixed relatives. On library plate 3 they sit in wells F11 and G11, directly next to GW early individuals (F-N; wells F10 and G10). Both were excluded from the genomic analyses within clades (`clades.exclude_samples` in the cluster config) and are not shown here; their phenotype data are kept. With them removed, no pair in any population reaches second-degree kinship.

```{r}
#| label: inbreeding
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
inb_files <- Sys.glob(cx("results", "06_relatedness", "inbreeding", "*.inbreed_samples.tsv"))
if (length(inb_files) == 0) {
  cat("Per-individual inbreeding (heterozygosity check) is not in this export yet.")
} else {
  inb <- map_dfr(inb_files, ~ read_tsv(.x, show_col_types = FALSE)) %>%
    inner_join(select(seq_data, sample_id, clade, site_code, season, mean_depth_nuclear), by = "sample_id") %>%
    filter(clade %in% tonsa_clades) %>%
    mutate(clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades),
           ord = match(as.character(site_code), site_order) * 10 + match(as.character(season), season_order),
           collection = fct_reorder(paste(site_code, season), ord)) %>%
    group_by(clade) %>%
    # flag only excess heterozygosity (low F); high F mostly reflects low depth (panel B)
    mutate(z = (F - median(F)) / mad(F), flag = z < -4) %>%   # robust z within clade
    ungroup()
  write_csv(inb, here("Output", "Output_data", "inbreeding_individuals.csv"))
  p_f <- ggplot(inb, aes(x = collection, y = F)) +
    facet_grid(~ clade, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
    geom_jitter(aes(colour = flag), width = 0.15, height = 0, size = 1.4, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(data = filter(inb, flag), aes(label = sample_id), size = 2.6, hjust = -0.1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey40", `TRUE` = "#B73534"), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Inbreeding coefficient F") +
    theme_matt_facets(base_size = 12) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  p_fd <- ggplot(inb, aes(x = mean_depth_nuclear, y = F, colour = clade)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.3, alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = clade_cols[tonsa_clades]) +
    labs(x = "Mean nuclear depth", y = "F", colour = "Clade") +
    theme_matt(base_size = 12)
  ggarrange(p_f, p_fd, nrow = 1, widths = c(2.2, 1), labels = "AUTO")
}
```

Per-individual inbreeding coefficients (PCAngsd, allowing for structure within each clade) flag libraries that are more heterozygous than expected (strongly negative F), the signature of DNA from two individuals in one library. Individuals more than 4 robust SDs below their clade's median are labelled. High F mostly reflects low sequencing depth (panel B: F falls with depth), so only unusually low values are informative. MR_peak_2_04 and MR_peak_2_05 (F = −0.18 and −0.22) were excluded on this basis and no longer appear; no other individual stands out.

### Local PCA and candidate inversions

Each clade's genome was split into windows of 2,000 SNPs, and the population structure in each window (top two PCs of the covariance among individuals) was compared between all windows (lostruct; Li & Ralph 2019). Windows were then placed on MDS axes: most of the genome shares the same structure and clusters near zero; regions with distinct structure, such as inversions, stand out as runs of windows far from zero. Windows more than 4 robust SDs from the median are coloured.

```{r}
#| label: localpca-genome
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 11
lp_files <- Sys.glob(cx("results", "08_localpca", "*", "windows.tsv"))
fai_file <- cx("data", "reference", "genome", "reference.fa.fai")
if (length(lp_files) == 0) {
  cat("Local PCA is not in this export yet.")
} else {
  chrom_order <- if (file.exists(fai_file)) read_tsv(fai_file, col_names = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE)$X1 else NULL
  lp <- map_dfr(lp_files, ~ read_tsv(.x, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
                  mutate(clade = basename(dirname(.x)))) %>%
    filter(clade %in% tonsa_clades)
  if (is.null(chrom_order)) chrom_order <- unique(lp$chrom)
  chroms <- intersect(chrom_order, unique(lp$chrom))
  lp <- lp %>%
    mutate(chr = factor(match(chrom, chroms)),
           mid_mb = (start + end) / 2e6,
           clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades)) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(mds1, mds2), names_to = "axis", values_to = "mds") %>%
    group_by(clade, axis) %>%
    mutate(z = (mds - median(mds)) / mad(mds), outlier = abs(z) > 4) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(row = factor(paste(clade, toupper(axis)),
                        levels = paste(rep(tonsa_clades, each = 2), c("MDS1", "MDS2"))))
  write_csv(lp, here("Output", "Output_data", "localpca_windows.csv"))
  ggplot(lp, aes(x = mid_mb, y = mds, colour = ifelse(outlier, as.character(clade), "none"))) +
    facet_grid(row ~ chr, scales = "free", space = "free_x", switch = "x") +
    geom_point(size = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(clade_cols[tonsa_clades], none = "grey70"), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Chromosome (window position)", y = "MDS coordinate") +
    theme_matt_facets(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(1, "pt"), strip.text.y = element_text(size = 9))
}
```

For each candidate region (at least 5 windows, mostly outliers), individuals are placed by their average PC1 score across the region's windows. An inversion typically splits individuals into three groups (the two homozygous arrangements and the heterozygotes); a region tracking site or sub-lineage instead points to differentiation, and a few individuals far from everyone else to a rare variant arrangement or introgression.

```{r}
#| label: localpca-regions
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 6
if (length(lp_files) > 0) {
  # candidate regions: runs of windows where >= 60% of the 5 surrounding windows are
  # outliers; runs separated by up to 3 windows are merged
  fill_gaps <- function(x, gap = 3) {
    r <- rle(x)
    inner <- seq_along(r$values) > 1 & seq_along(r$values) < length(r$values)
    r$values[!r$values & r$lengths <= gap & inner] <- TRUE
    inverse.rle(r)
  }
  regions <- lp %>%
    arrange(clade, axis, chr, start) %>%
    group_by(clade, axis, chr) %>%
    mutate(dens = map_dbl(seq_along(outlier), ~ mean(outlier[max(1, .x - 2):min(length(outlier), .x + 2)])),
           inreg = fill_gaps(dens >= 0.6),
           run = cumsum(inreg != lag(inreg, default = FALSE))) %>%
    filter(inreg) %>%
    group_by(clade, axis, chr, run) %>%
    summarise(chrom = first(chrom), start = min(start), end = max(end), n_win = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n_win >= 5) %>%
    arrange(clade, as.integer(as.character(chr)), start) %>%
    mutate(label = sprintf("%s chr%s: %.1f–%.1f Mb (%s, %d windows)", clade, chr, start / 1e6, end / 1e6,
                           toupper(axis), n_win))
  write_csv(regions, here("Output", "Output_data", "localpca_candidate_regions.csv"))
  if (nrow(regions) == 0) {
    cat("No candidate regions (runs of at least 5 outlier windows).")
  } else {
    region_scores <- pmap_dfr(regions, function(clade, chrom, start, end, label, ...) {
      sc <- read_tsv(cx("results", "08_localpca", clade, "window_pc1_scores.tsv.gz"), show_col_types = FALSE)
      m <- sc %>% filter(chrom == !!chrom, start >= !!start, end <= !!end) %>% select(-chrom, -start, -end) %>% as.matrix()
      ref <- m[which.max(rowSums(abs(m))), ]
      m <- m * sign(apply(m, 1, function(x) cor(x, ref)))      # PC signs are arbitrary per window
      tibble(label = label, clade = clade, sample_id = colnames(m), score = colMeans(m))
    }) %>%
      left_join(select(seq_data, sample_id, site_code, season), by = "sample_id") %>%
      mutate(site_code = factor(site_code, levels = site_order),
             label = factor(label, levels = regions$label))
    ggplot(region_scores, aes(x = score, y = site_code, fill = site_code)) +
      facet_wrap(~ label, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
      geom_jitter(shape = 21, size = 2, height = 0.2, width = 0, colour = "grey20", stroke = 0.2) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = pop_cols[site_order], guide = "none") +
      labs(x = "Mean PC1 score across the region", y = NULL) +
      theme_matt_facets(base_size = 12)
  }
}
```


#### Follow-up of the candidate regions

Each candidate region (and a control region on chromosome 1 with no local-PCA signal) was analysed on its own: a PCA of the region (PCAngsd), each individual's heterozygosity inside the region relative to its genome-wide heterozygosity, and LD over distances up to 2 Mb. An inversion shows as groups on the regional PC1 with heterozygotes raised in heterozygosity (ratio above the bulk) and homozygotes for the rarer arrangement lowered; suppressed recombination raises long-range LD when both arrangements are common.

```{r}
#| label: region-followup
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 9
reg_dirs <- Sys.glob(cx("results", "11_regions", "*"))
reg_dirs <- reg_dirs[file.exists(file.path(reg_dirs, "het.tsv"))]
if (length(reg_dirs) == 0) {
  cat("Candidate-region results are not in this export yet.")
} else {
  reg <- map_dfr(reg_dirs, function(d) {
    region <- basename(d)
    clade <- sub("_.*", "", region)
    ids <- readLines(cx("results", "02_sites", "bamlists", paste0(clade, ".ids.txt")))
    cv <- as.matrix(read.table(file.path(d, "pcangsd.cov")))
    e <- eigen(cv, symmetric = TRUE)
    het <- read_tsv(file.path(d, "het.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
    tibble(region = region, sample_id = ids, PC1 = e$vectors[, 1], PC2 = e$vectors[, 2],
           pc1_pct = 100 * e$values[1] / sum(e$values)) %>%
      left_join(het, by = "sample_id")
  }) %>%
    left_join(select(seq_data, sample_id, site_code, season), by = "sample_id") %>%
    group_by(region) %>%
    mutate(PC1 = PC1 * sign(sum(PC1^3)) * -1,                      # put the minority group on the left
           z_het = (het_ratio - median(het_ratio)) / mad(het_ratio),
           # label a small group far from the rest on PC1 (< 15% of individuals), and the
           # 2 most extreme individuals for heterozygosity
           far = abs(PC1 - median(PC1)) > 0.15,
           label = if_else((far & mean(far) < 0.15) | rank(het_ratio) <= 2 | rank(-het_ratio) <= 2,
                           sample_id, NA_character_),
           panel = sprintf("%s (PC1 %.1f%%)", region, first(pc1_pct))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(site_code = factor(site_code, levels = site_order))
  write_csv(reg, here("Output", "Output_data", "candidate_regions_individuals.csv"))

  p_reg <- ggplot(reg, aes(x = PC1, y = het_ratio, fill = site_code)) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free", nrow = 1) +
    geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2.2, colour = "grey20", stroke = 0.2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.6, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pop_cols[site_order], drop = TRUE) +
    labs(x = "Regional PC1", y = "Heterozygosity in region / genome-wide", fill = "Site") +
    theme_matt_facets(base_size = 12)

  reg_ld <- map_dfr(reg_dirs, ~ read_tsv(file.path(.x, "ld_bins.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
                      mutate(region = basename(.x))) %>%
    filter(n_pairs >= 50)
  p_ld <- ggplot(reg_ld, aes(x = min_bp / 1000, y = mean_r2_ExpG, colour = region)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey55", "#24518B", "#B73534")) +
    labs(x = "Distance between SNPs (kb, log scale)", y = expression(Mean~italic(r)^2), colour = NULL) +
    theme_matt(base_size = 12)

  ggarrange(p_reg, ggarrange(p_ld, NULL, widths = c(1, 1.2)), nrow = 2, heights = c(1.2, 1), labels = c("A", "B"))
}
```

**Chromosome 6 (X)** fits a rare chromosomal variant such as an inversion. A minority of individuals, almost all from St. Thomas de Kent Wharf and a few from Ritchie Wharf, sits apart on the regional PC1. Most of them are about 5% more heterozygous on chromosome 6 than their genome-wide average, as expected for heterozygous carriers, while the two most extreme individuals (TK_peak_1_09, TK_peak_2_07) are less heterozygous, as expected for homozygotes of the rare arrangement. At this frequency (roughly 5% of chromosomes overall) LD across the whole sample is raised only slightly (panel B: higher at short distances and marginally at 0.1–2 Mb than on the control chromosome). **Chromosome 3 (X)** does not: individuals split by site as on the control chromosome, with no heterozygosity classes; only two or three TK early individuals stand out on PC2 with slightly raised heterozygosity, which could be a smaller rare variant within the region.

### Parasites and symbionts

Reads that did not map to the *A. tonsa* reference were screened for small-subunit rRNA (phyloFlash, SILVA 138.1). Each read pair was assigned to the shared ancestor of all equally good database hits, at a rank limited by its identity, and host (*Acartia*) rRNA was removed. An organism group was called present at ≥ 5 read pairs and ≥ 2 per million library pairs (`Scripts/04_micro_calls.R`). Parasites (*Paradinium*, trematodes) and epibionts (apostome and peritrich ciliates) show strong site × season patterns: apostomes in every Connecticut late-season individual, trematodes in most Ritchie Wharf peak-season individuals, and *Zoothamnium* on late-season Maine and St. Thomas de Kent Wharf copepods.

```{r}
#| label: micro-setup
#| include: false

micro_labels <- c(paradinium = "Paradinium (parasite)", trematode = "Hemiuroid trematodes",
                  apostome = "Apostome ciliates", peritrich = "Peritrich ciliates (Zoothamnium)",
                  cnidaria_myxozoa = "Cnidaria / Myxozoa", kinetoplastid = "Kinetoplastids (background)",
                  malacostraca = "Malacostraca (diet)")

  filter(clade %in% tonsa_clades, !library_failed) %>%
  select(sample_id, site_code, season, clade, ends_with("_call"), ends_with("_per_M")) %>%

               names_to = c("group", ".value"), names_pattern = "(.*)_(call|per_M)") %>%
  filter(group %in% names(micro_labels))

micro_prev <- function(groups) {

    filter(group %in% groups) %>%
    group_by(group, site_code, season) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), k = sum(call), .groups = "drop") %>%
    complete(group = groups, site_code = factor(site_order, levels = levels(site_code)),
             season = factor(season_order, levels = season_order)) %>%
    mutate(prev = k / n,
           group = factor(micro_labels[group], levels = rev(micro_labels[groups])),
           site_code = factor(site_code, levels = site_order))
}

    geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, !is.na(n), k == 0), shape = 1, size = 1.5, colour = "grey75") +
    geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, k > 0), aes(size = prev), colour = "grey15") +

              nudge_y = -0.35, size = 3, colour = "grey45") +

strip_plot <- function(groups) {
  d <- micro_ind %>%
    filter(group %in% groups) %>%
    arrange(site_code, season, clade) %>%
    mutate(sample_id = factor(sample_id, levels = unique(sample_id)),

           per_M = na_if(per_M, 0))
  bar <- distinct(d, sample_id, clade, site_code, season) %>%
```

### Seasonal allele-frequency change

Allele frequencies per population at the unlinked SNP set (one SNP per 10 kb; Section 3.2, LD) were compared between seasons within each site. Temporal differentiation is Nei & Tajima's F<sub>c</sub> ([Nei & Tajima 1981](https://doi.org/10.1093/genetics/98.3.625)) over SNPs with ≥ 5 individuals with data in both samples and a mean minor-allele frequency of 0.05–0.95. Under the temporal method, F<sub>c</sub> ≈ t/(2N<sub>e</sub>) + sampling noise of both samples, so N<sub>e</sub> follows once the sampling noise is subtracted ([Waples 1989](https://doi.org/10.1093/genetics/121.2.379); [Jorde & Ryman 2007](https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.107.075481)).

**Calibrating sampling noise.** With < 1× coverage, frequencies are sampled twice, once through the individuals and once through the reads, so an individual contributes less than two chromosomes of information ([Jónás et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.116.191197)). Pool-seq studies handle this with an "effective number of chromosomes" ([Feder et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0048588); [Bergland et al. 2014](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgen.1004775); [Machado et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.67577)). Here it was measured directly: each population was split at random into two halves (two replicates), allele frequencies were estimated for each half, and F<sub>c</sub> between the halves (pure sampling noise) was compared with the 1/(2n) expectation. The ratio, c, is the effective number of chromosomes per individual divided by two, and the sampling term for any sample becomes 1/(2cn). This split-half calibration is an empirical resampling check rather than a named published method.

```{r}
#| label: split-half
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
split_half <- read_cx("results", "12_split", "split_half.tsv")
if (is.null(split_half)) {
  cat("Split-half calibration is not in this export yet.")
} else {
  c_pop <- split_half %>%
    group_by(population) %>%
    summarise(c = mean(c), c_diff = abs(diff(range(c))), n = mean(mean_n_a + mean_n_b), .groups = "drop") %>%
    separate(population, c("clade", "site", "season"), sep = "__", remove = FALSE) %>%
    filter(clade %in% tonsa_clades) %>%
    mutate(clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades),
           label = paste(site, season))
  ggplot(c_pop, aes(x = reorder(label, c), y = c, colour = clade)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    facet_grid(. ~ clade, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = clade_cols[tonsa_clades], guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.05)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "c (effective chromosomes\nper individual / 2)",
         caption = "Mean of two random splits per population; dashed line = two full chromosomes per individual") +
    theme_matt_facets(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}
```

Every population gives c ≈ 0.6–0.7 (about 1.2–1.4 effective chromosomes per individual), and the two random splits agree to within 0.02. The calibration is therefore stable and similar across clades, sites and seasons.

```{r}
#| label: seasonal-change
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5
freq_files <- Sys.glob(cx("results", "09_stage34", "*.freqs.unlinked.tsv.gz"))
if (length(freq_files) == 0 || !exists("generations") || is.null(split_half)) {
  cat("Allele-frequency tables or the split-half calibration are not in this export yet.")
} else {
  season_lv <- c("early", "peak", "late")
  c_of <- setNames(c_pop$c, c_pop$population)
  gens_tab <- generations %>% ungroup() %>%
    left_join(distinct(site_data, site, site_code), by = "site") %>%
    select(site_code, season, gens)
  gens_between <- function(site, s1, s2) {
    steps <- c("early_to_peak", "peak_to_late")[match(s1, season_lv):(match(s2, season_lv) - 1)]
    g <- gens_tab$gens[gens_tab$site_code == site & gens_tab$season %in% steps]
    if (length(g) == length(steps)) sum(g) else NA_real_
  }
  # Fc, uncalibrated (2 chromosomes per individual) and calibrated sampling terms, and
  # a delete-one-chromosome jackknife SE of the calibrated excess
  fc_pair <- function(m, a, b, min_n = 5) {
    x <- m[[paste0("freq_", a)]]; y <- m[[paste0("freq_", b)]]
    na <- m[[paste0("nind_", a)]]; nb <- m[[paste0("nind_", b)]]
    z <- (x + y) / 2
    ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(y) & na >= min_n & nb >= min_n & z >= 0.05 & z <= 0.95
    x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]; z <- z[ok]; na <- na[ok]; nb <- nb[ok]; ch <- m$chrom[ok]
    excess <- function(k) sum((x[k] - y[k])^2) / sum(z[k] - x[k] * y[k]) -
      mean(1 / (2 * c_of[[a]] * na[k]) + 1 / (2 * c_of[[b]] * nb[k]))
    jk <- map_dbl(unique(ch), ~ excess(ch != .x)); g <- length(jk)
    Fc <- sum((x - y)^2) / sum(z - x * y)
    tibble(snps = sum(ok), Fc = Fc,
           sampling_2n = mean(1 / (2 * na) + 1 / (2 * nb)),
           sampling_cal = Fc - excess(rep(TRUE, length(x))),
           excess = Fc - sampling_cal,
           se = sqrt((g - 1) / g * sum((jk - mean(jk))^2)))
  }
  temporal <- map_dfr(freq_files, function(f) {
    clade <- sub("\\.freqs.*", "", basename(f))
    m <- read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(chrom = "c"))
    pops <- sub("^freq_", "", grep("^freq_", names(m), value = TRUE))
    combn(pops, 2, simplify = FALSE) %>% map_dfr(function(p) {
      a <- str_split_1(p[1], "__"); b <- str_split_1(p[2], "__")
      if (a[2] != b[2]) return(NULL)                       # seasonal pairs only
      ord <- order(match(c(a[3], b[3]), season_lv)); pp <- p[ord]
      s <- c(a[3], b[3])[ord]
      bind_cols(tibble(clade = clade, site = a[2], from = s[1], to = s[2],
                       gens = gens_between(a[2], s[1], s[2])),
                fc_pair(m, pp[1], pp[2]))
    })
  }) %>%
    mutate(ne = if_else(excess > 0, gens / (2 * excess), Inf),
           ne_lo = gens / (2 * (excess + 1.96 * se)),
           ne_hi = if_else(excess - 1.96 * se > 0, gens / (2 * (excess - 1.96 * se)), Inf),
           clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades),
           pair = paste0(site, " ", from, "→", to))
  write_csv(temporal, here("Output", "Output_data", "temporal_fc.csv"))

  p_exc <- temporal %>%
    mutate(uncal = Fc - sampling_2n) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = gens, colour = clade)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(aes(y = uncal), shape = 1, size = 2.5, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(y = excess, ymin = excess - 1.96 * se, ymax = excess + 1.96 * se), size = 0.5) +
    geom_text(aes(y = excess, label = pair), size = 2.8, vjust = -1.2, check_overlap = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = clade_cols[tonsa_clades]) +
    labs(x = "Generations between samples", y = expression(F[c] - "sampling noise"),
         colour = "Clade",
         caption = "Open circles: sampling noise assuming 2 chromosomes per individual.\nFilled: calibrated sampling noise (1/2cn), ± 95% CI from a chromosome jackknife.") +
    theme_matt(base_size = 12)
  p_exc
}
```

```{r}
#| label: seasonal-ne-table
if (exists("temporal")) {
  temporal %>%
    transmute(Clade = clade, Pair = pair, Generations = gens, SNPs = snps,
              Fc = round(Fc, 3), `Excess (calibrated)` = sprintf("%.4f ± %.4f", excess, se),
              Ne = if_else(is.finite(ne), sprintf("%.0f", ne), "∞"),
              `Ne 95% CI` = sprintf("%.0f – %s", ne_lo, if_else(is.finite(ne_hi), sprintf("%.0f", ne_hi), "∞"))) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = "Temporal F~c~ and N~e~ per seasonal pair, with sampling noise calibrated by the split-half c. CI from a delete-one-chromosome jackknife of the excess; ∞ = excess not distinguishable from zero.")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: seasonal-parallel
if (exists("temporal")) {
  # parallel change: correlation of early→peak changes between X sites
  mx <- read_tsv(cx("results", "09_stage34", "X.freqs.unlinked.tsv.gz"), show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(chrom = "c"))
  dp <- function(site, s1, s2) {
    a <- paste0("X__", site, "__", s1); b <- paste0("X__", site, "__", s2)
    ok <- mx[[paste0("nind_", a)]] >= 5 & mx[[paste0("nind_", b)]] >= 5
    if_else(ok, mx[[paste0("freq_", b)]] - mx[[paste0("freq_", a)]], NA_real_)
  }
  d <- tibble(chrom = mx$chrom, ME = dp("ME", "early", "peak"), TK = dp("TK", "early", "peak"),
              RW = dp("RW", "early", "peak")) %>% drop_na()
  par_tab <- map_dfr(list(c("ME", "TK"), c("ME", "RW"), c("TK", "RW")), function(p) {
    r <- cor(d[[p[1]]], d[[p[2]]])
    jk <- map_dbl(unique(d$chrom), function(ch) { k <- d$chrom != ch; cor(d[[p[1]]][k], d[[p[2]]][k]) })
    g <- length(jk)
    tibble(comparison = paste(p, collapse = " vs "), snps = nrow(d), r = r,
           se = sqrt((g - 1) / g * sum((jk - mean(jk))^2)))
  })
  knitr::kable(par_tab, digits = 3,
               caption = "Clade X: correlation of early→peak allele-frequency change between sites (unlinked SNPs; SE from a delete-one-chromosome jackknife)")
}
```

Calibration removes almost all of the apparent excess: with two chromosomes per individual assumed, every pair showed an excess of ≈ 0.05 regardless of the number of generations (open circles); with the calibrated sampling term the excess is 0.000–0.011 (filled points). Most pairs give N<sub>e</sub> in the high hundreds to a few thousand, with lower 95% bounds of roughly 400–2,000, and several upper bounds are infinite (no drift detectable within the season). These estimates describe drift over a few to ~20 generations within one season, not long-term N<sub>e</sub>, and they are at or above the lab estimate of ~400. ME early→peak is the exception (N<sub>e</sub> ≈ 225, CI ≈ 185–285): ME early is the smallest X sample (10 individuals), so a modest error in its c would inflate the excess, and the value should be checked before it is interpreted biologically. In clade X, early→peak changes at different sites remain uncorrelated genome-wide (r ≈ 0).

**Per-SNP seasonal test.** For each SNP, the minor-allele count was modelled with a binomial GLM, count ~ site + x, with each population weighted by its effective number of chromosomes (2cn), as in the *Drosophila* seasonal studies ([Bergland et al. 2014](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgen.1004775); [Machado et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.67577)). Two versions of x were fitted: (1) **time**, the collection day of year scaled from 0 (first sampling event at a site) to 1 (last), which rewards change in the same direction through the season at every site; and (2) **temperature**, the mean MUR SST over the generation before each collection (Ganey's Wharf corrected against station ET5.1), which rewards change that tracks temperature, so that a warming and a cooling step move frequencies in opposite directions. Temperature matters because the season is not a monotonic temperature ramp: water before the early and peak collections was similar (or cooler at peak in the north), and the late collections followed a strong cooling. The null distribution comes from permuting x among each site's sampling events, enumerating every distinct ordering (time: X 11 and F 23 permutations, as reversing all sites only flips the sign; temperature: X 23 and F 47). The genome-wide test asks whether more SNPs reach a given p value with the real values than with the permuted ones. Results are shown with and without chromosome 6, which carries the likely inversion in clade X (Section 3.2). Clade S has a single seasonal site (MD) with two samples, so it has no permutation null and is not shown.

```{r}
#| label: seasonal-glm
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5
glm_files <- c(Sys.glob(cx("results", "13_seasonal", "*.perm.tsv")),
               Sys.glob(cx("results", "13_seasonal", "temp", "*.perm.tsv")))
if (length(glm_files) == 0) {
  cat("Seasonal GLM results are not in this export yet.")
} else {
  glm_perm <- map_dfr(glm_files, function(f) {
    read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(clade = str_split_1(basename(f), "\\.")[1], snps_used = str_split_1(basename(f), "\\.")[2],
             model = if_else(basename(dirname(f)) == "temp", "temperature", "time"))
  }) %>%
    filter(clade %in% c("X", "F")) %>%
    mutate(snp_set = if_else(snp_set == "all", "all chr.", "no chr6"),
           model = factor(model, levels = c("time", "temperature")),
           panel = paste0(clade, ", ", snps_used, " SNPs"),
           clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades)) %>%
    pivot_longer(starts_with("n_p<"), names_to = "threshold", values_to = "n_snps") %>%
    mutate(threshold = sub("n_", "", threshold), observed = perm == 0)

  glm_perm %>%
    filter(threshold %in% c("p<0.01", "p<0.001"), snp_set == "all chr.") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = model, y = n_snps)) +
    geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, !observed), colour = "grey60", alpha = 0.7,
               position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, seed = 1)) +
    geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, observed), aes(colour = clade), size = 3.5, shape = 18) +
    facet_wrap(threshold ~ panel, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = clade_cols[tonsa_clades], guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "SNPs below threshold",
         caption = "Diamonds: observed. Grey: every within-site reordering of the sampling events. All chromosomes (with/without chr6 in the table).") +
    theme_matt_facets(base_size = 11)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: seasonal-glm-table
if (length(glm_files) > 0) {
  glm_perm %>%
    group_by(clade, snps_used, model, snp_set, threshold) %>%
    summarise(obs = n_snps[observed], perm_mean = mean(n_snps[!observed]),
              perm_max = max(n_snps[!observed]),
              rank = sum(n_snps[!observed] >= n_snps[observed]) + 1, label_sets = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(rank = paste0(rank, " / ", label_sets)) %>%
    select(-label_sets) %>%
    arrange(clade, snps_used, model, snp_set, threshold) %>%
    knitr::kable(digits = 1, col.names = c("Clade", "SNPs", "Model", "Chromosomes", "Threshold", "Observed",
                                          "Permutation mean", "Permutation max", "Rank of observed"),
                 caption = "Per-SNP seasonal GLM: SNPs below each p threshold with the real seasons vs all within-site permutations (rank 1 = more than every permutation).")
}
```

There is no genome-wide excess of seasonal SNPs in either clade, with either model. With the real seasons, X and F have about as many low-p SNPs as the permuted orderings, at every threshold, on both the unlinked and the full SNP sets. Modelling temperature instead of time does not change this: the closest to a signal is clade X on all SNPs (rank 5–6 of 24 at p < 0.01 and p < 0.001, i.e. p ≈ 0.2–0.25), which is not significant and does not hold on the unlinked set. Removing chromosome 6 changes nothing, so the X inversion is not driving or masking a seasonal signal. The genomic-control λ is close to 1 (X ≈ 1.1, F ≈ 1.0) for the observed and permuted values alike, so the calibrated binomial weights describe the sampling variance well. Together with the uncorrelated early→peak changes across X sites, this means that any seasonal selection in these populations acts on too few loci, or is too weak, to show up genome-wide with 3–4 seasonal sites per clade, whether it is modelled as a seasonal trend or as a response to temperature. Individual SNPs with the smallest p values are listed in `results/13_seasonal/*.top.tsv` and `results/13_seasonal/temp/*.top.tsv` but are not more numerous than expected by chance, so none can be called a seasonal candidate on its own. The permutation null is coarse (time: 12 and 24 orderings; temperature: 24 and 48), which limits the smallest attainable rank-based p value to 1/12–1/48.



### Spatial vs. seasonal genetic variation

How much do allele frequencies differ between sites compared with between seasons at the same site? Within each clade, the variance of population allele frequencies at the unlinked SNPs was split into a between-site component and a between-season (within-site) component, after subtracting the calibrated sampling noise (1/(2cn) per population, from the split-half calibration). Both are expressed relative to p̄(1 − p̄), like F<sub>ST</sub>, summed over SNPs (ratio of sums), with 95% intervals from a delete-one-chromosome jackknife. The between-site component reflects long-term history and spatial selection; the seasonal component reflects drift and selection over a single season (3–20 generations).

```{r}
#| label: freq-variance-partition
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
if (length(freq_files) == 0 || is.null(split_half)) {
  cat("Allele-frequency tables or the split-half calibration are not in this export yet.")
} else {
  # population sets (clade.prefix = which frequency table): F-N = F populations at MD and GW;
  # F as a whole spans three lineages (its between-site component includes lineage divergence)
  vp_sets <- list(X = c("X", NA), S = c("S", NA), IV = c("IV", NA), `F-N` = c("F", "MD|GW"), `F (all lineages)` = c("F", NA))
  vp_freq <- map_dfr(names(vp_sets), function(nm) {
    cl <- vp_sets[[nm]][1]; site_pat <- vp_sets[[nm]][2]
    f <- cx("results", "09_stage34", paste0(cl, ".freqs.unlinked.tsv.gz"))
    if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
    m <- read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(chrom = "c"))
    pops <- sub("^freq_", "", grep("^freq_", names(m), value = TRUE))
    site <- str_split_i(pops, "__", 2)
    if (!is.na(site_pat)) { keep <- str_detect(site, paste0("^(", site_pat, ")$")); pops <- pops[keep]; site <- site[keep] }
    P <- as.matrix(m[paste0("freq_", pops)]); N <- as.matrix(m[paste0("nind_", pops)])
    cvec <- unname(c_of[pops]); cvec[is.na(cvec)] <- median(c_of)
    ok <- rowSums(is.na(P)) == 0 & rowSums(N < 5, na.rm = TRUE) == 0 & rowSums(is.na(N)) == 0
    pbar <- rowMeans(P); ok <- ok & pbar >= 0.05 & pbar <= 0.95
    P <- P[ok, , drop = FALSE]; N <- N[ok, , drop = FALSE]; pbar <- pbar[ok]; chrom <- m$chrom[ok]
    # sampling variance of each population's frequency, from its own frequency:
    # E[p(1-p)] = p(1-p)(1 - 1/n_eff), so p(1-p) / (n_eff - 1) is unbiased; n_eff = 2cn chromosomes
    neff <- 2 * sweep(N, 2, cvec, "*")
    s2 <- P * (1 - P) / pmax(neff - 1, 1)
    sites <- unique(site); I <- length(sites); k <- table(site)[sites]
    # within-site (seasonal) component
    W <- 0; EW <- 0
    msite <- sapply(sites, function(s) rowMeans(P[, site == s, drop = FALSE]))
    if (!is.matrix(msite)) msite <- matrix(msite, ncol = I)
    s2bar <- sapply(sites, function(s) rowMeans(s2[, site == s, drop = FALSE]))
    if (!is.matrix(s2bar)) s2bar <- matrix(s2bar, ncol = I)
    for (j in seq_along(sites)) {
      cols <- which(site == sites[j])
      W <- W + rowSums((P[, cols, drop = FALSE] - msite[, j])^2)
      EW <- EW + rowSums(s2[, cols, drop = FALSE]) * (1 - 1 / k[[j]])
    }
    df_w <- sum(k - 1)
    sig_season <- if (df_w > 0) (W - EW) / df_w else rep(NA_real_, length(pbar))
    # between-site component
    sig_site <- if (I > 1) {
      B <- rowSums((msite - rowMeans(msite))^2)
      adj <- rowSums(sweep(s2bar, 2, as.numeric(k), "/")) + (if (df_w > 0) sig_season else 0) * sum(1 / k)
      (B - (1 - 1 / I) * adj) / (I - 1)
    } else rep(NA_real_, length(pbar))
    het <- pbar * (1 - pbar)
    est <- function(sel) c(site = sum(sig_site[sel]) / sum(het[sel]), season = sum(sig_season[sel]) / sum(het[sel]))
    full <- est(rep(TRUE, length(pbar)))
    jk <- sapply(unique(chrom), function(ch) est(chrom != ch)); g <- ncol(jk)
    se <- sqrt((g - 1) / g * rowSums((jk - rowMeans(jk))^2))
    tibble(group = nm, component = c("Between sites", "Between seasons (within site)"),
           value = unname(full), lo = unname(full - 1.96 * se), hi = unname(full + 1.96 * se),
           sites = I, populations = length(pops), seasonal_sites = sum(k > 1), snps = length(pbar))
  }) %>%
    mutate(group = factor(group, levels = names(vp_sets)))

  ggplot(filter(vp_freq, !is.na(value), group != "F (all lineages)"), aes(x = group, y = value, colour = component)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`Between sites` = unname(lat_gradient["MR"]),
                                   `Between seasons (within site)` = unname(lat_gradient["X"])), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = expression("Variance / " * bar(p) * "(1 - " * bar(p) * ")"),
         caption = "Unlinked SNPs; sampling noise removed; 95% CI: chromosome jackknife.\nF across all lineages is in the table only (its between-site variance is lineage divergence).") +
    theme_matt(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: freq-variance-partition-table
if (exists("vp_freq")) {
  vp_freq %>%
    mutate(value = if_else(is.na(value), "–", sprintf("%.4f (%.4f, %.4f)", value, lo, hi))) %>%
    select(group, component, value, sites, seasonal_sites, populations, snps) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = component, values_from = value) %>%
    mutate(`Site : season ratio` = map2_chr(group, sites, function(g, s) {
      v <- filter(vp_freq, group == g)
      se <- v[v$component == "Between seasons (within site)", ]
      if (any(is.na(v$value)) || se$lo <= 0) "–" else
        sprintf("%.0f", v$value[v$component == "Between sites"] / se$value)
    })) %>%
    knitr::kable(col.names = c("Group", "Sites", "Sites with ≥ 2 seasons", "Populations", "SNPs",
                               "Between sites", "Between seasons", "Site : season ratio"),
                 caption = "Allele-frequency variance between sites and between seasons within sites, relative to p̄(1 − p̄), after removing sampling noise (95% CI). Ratio shown only where the seasonal component is clearly above zero.")
}
```

```{r}
#| include: false
vf <- function(g, comp, what = "value") filter(vp_freq, group == g, component == comp)[[what]]
```

Allele frequencies differ far more between sites than between seasons at the same site. In clade X, the between-site variance (`r sprintf("%.3f", vf("X", "Between sites"))`) is about `r round(vf("X", "Between sites") / vf("X", "Between seasons (within site)"))` times the seasonal variance (`r sprintf("%.4f", vf("X", "Between seasons (within site)"))`); in F-N (MD vs. GW) the ratio is about `r round(vf("F-N", "Between sites") / vf("F-N", "Between seasons (within site)"))`. The seasonal component is small but above zero in X and F-N, consistent with the temporal F<sub>c</sub> excess above (drift over a season with N<sub>e</sub> in the high hundreds to thousands); in S, with one seasonal site, it is indistinguishable from zero. Across the F lineages the between-site component (`r sprintf("%.2f", vf("F (all lineages)", "Between sites"))`) is an order of magnitude larger, because it measures divergence between lineages rather than among populations of one lineage. Seasonal change in allele frequencies is therefore a small fraction of the spatial differentiation it would have to reproduce for seasonal evolution to mirror spatial adaptation, which fits the absence of concordance below.


### Does space substitute for time? Concordance of temperature responses

If the alleles that are more common at warmer sites are favoured by warm conditions, they should also rise after warm periods and fall after cool ones within sites. For every SNP, two temperature slopes were estimated with the same binomial GLM and calibrated weights as above: a **spatial** slope (frequency against each site's long-term MUR SST, with a site's seasonal samples pooled) and a **seasonal** slope (the temperature model above: frequency against site + temperature before collection). Their agreement across the genome was measured as the correlation of the two z-scores, and, among the 1% and 5% of SNPs with the strongest spatial slopes, as the fraction whose seasonal slope has the same sign (0.5 = no agreement). The null keeps the spatial slopes and permutes temperatures among each site's sampling events (as in the seasonal test); a second, smaller null permutes site temperatures among sites. This is the genomic counterpart of the within- vs between-site comparison for CTmax (Section 4) and follows the seasonal–clinal comparison of [Machado et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.67577).

Clade X (ME, TK, RW; one lineage, three seasonal sites) is the main test. In clade F the warm sites (MR, FH) and the cool sites (MD, GW) belong to different lineages, so its spatial slopes mostly reflect lineage differences, not temperature; F is shown for completeness but not interpreted. Clade S has one seasonal site, so its seasonal null has a single alternative ordering.

```{r}
#| label: concordance
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.5
conc_files <- Sys.glob(cx("results", "14_concordance", "*.perm.tsv"))
if (length(conc_files) == 0) {
  cat("Concordance results are not in this export yet.")
} else {
  conc <- map_dfr(conc_files, function(f) {
    read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(clade = str_split_1(basename(f), "\\.")[1], snps_used = str_split_1(basename(f), "\\.")[2])
  }) %>%
    mutate(snp_set = if_else(snp_set == "all", "all chr.", "no chr6"),
           clade = factor(clade, levels = tonsa_clades),
           observed = null == "seasonal" & perm == 0)

  conc %>%
    filter(snp_set == "all chr.", null == "seasonal") %>%
    select(clade, snps_used, observed, r, conc_top1, conc_top5) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(r, conc_top1, conc_top5), names_to = "statistic", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(statistic = recode(statistic, r = "Correlation of z-scores",
                              conc_top1 = "Same direction, top 1% spatial SNPs",
                              conc_top5 = "Same direction, top 5% spatial SNPs"),
           x = paste(clade, snps_used, sep = "\n")) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = x, y = value)) +
    geom_hline(data = tibble(statistic = c("Correlation of z-scores", "Same direction, top 1% spatial SNPs",
                                           "Same direction, top 5% spatial SNPs"), h = c(0, 0.5, 0.5)),
               aes(yintercept = h), colour = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, !observed), colour = "grey60", alpha = 0.7,
               position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, seed = 1)) +
    geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, observed), aes(colour = str_sub(x, 1, 1)), size = 3.5, shape = 18) +
    facet_wrap(~ statistic, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(clade_cols[c("F", "S", "X")], c("F", "S", "X")), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
         caption = "Diamonds: observed. Grey: seasonal null (temperatures permuted among each site's sampling events). All chromosomes.") +
    theme_matt_facets(base_size = 11)
}
```
