```{r}
#| label: concordance-table
if (length(conc_files) > 0) {
  conc %>%
    filter(null == "seasonal") %>%
    group_by(clade, snps_used, snp_set) %>%
    summarise(snps = snps[observed],
              r_obs = r[observed], r_rank = sum(r[!observed] >= r[observed]) + 1,
              top1_obs = conc_top1[observed], top1_rank = sum(conc_top1[!observed] >= conc_top1[observed]) + 1,
              top5_obs = conc_top5[observed], top5_rank = sum(conc_top5[!observed] >= conc_top5[observed]) + 1,
              sets = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(across(ends_with("_rank"), ~ paste0(.x, " / ", sets))) %>%
    select(-sets) %>%
    arrange(clade, snps_used, snp_set) %>%
    knitr::kable(digits = 3,
                 col.names = c("Clade", "SNPs", "Chromosomes", "SNPs tested", "r", "Rank",
                               "Top 1% same sign", "Rank", "Top 5% same sign", "Rank"),
                 caption = "Concordance of spatial and seasonal temperature slopes. Rank = position of the observed value among all seasonal-null orderings (1 = higher than every permutation).")
}
```

In clade X the spatial and seasonal responses point weakly in the same direction: across all SNPs the two slopes are slightly positively correlated (r ≈ 0.04), and among the 1% of SNPs with the strongest spatial slopes about 55% change in the same direction through the season. But the real temperatures rank only 5th–6th of 24 orderings (p ≈ 0.2), 8th–12th on the unlinked set, and the smaller spatial null (6 orderings) cannot go below p ≈ 0.17; removing chromosome 6 changes nothing. So there is no detectable genome-wide concordance between spatial and seasonal temperature responses. Two limits shape this answer. First, the spatial temperature contrast within X is short (7.1–9.9 °C long-term mean across ME, TK and RW), and the spatial slope is mostly ME against the two Gulf of St. Lawrence sites, so it also carries their geographic separation. Second, the null rests on only 24 orderings. A modest true concordance, of the size seen here, could go undetected. Clade F shows the opposite tendency (its observed concordance is the lowest of 48 orderings for the top-1% statistic), but because its spatial contrast is a contrast between lineages (Florida lineages vs F-N) it is not interpreted as a temperature response. Clade S has no usable seasonal null.

In contrast to CTmax, whose between-site slope matches the within-site (acclimation) slope (Section 4), allele frequencies give no evidence that the response to temperature across sites predicts the response through the season. The genomic side of the space-for-time question therefore remains unresolved rather than negative: the data are consistent with no shared response and with a weak one.


## 4. Clade-specific physiological patterns

### CTmax model

To more formally test the relationship between CTmax and collection temperature, we used a linear mixed effects model, structured as `ctmax ~ clade * temp_cent + (1 | site) + (1 | replicate) + (1 | tube)`. This examines the effects of clade and temperature on CTmax, along with clade-specific effects of temperature. Body size is not included, so temperature effects include any effect acting through body size. Collection temperature was centered before model fitting. The model also includes random intercepts for each site, the assay run (replicate) and the tube number (the position of each individual within the water bath during the CTmax assay).

```{r}
#| label: ctmax-model
#| include: false
filtered_data = join_data %>% 
  filter(clade != "A_hudsonica") %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  drop_na(size, ctmax) %>% 
  mutate(ctmax_cent = scale(ctmax, scale = F)[,1],
         temp_cent = scale(collection_temp, scale = F)[,1],
         size_cent = scale(size, scale = F)[,1],
         sal_cent = scale(collection_salinity, scale = F)[,1],
         sal_type = if_else(collection_salinity > 15, "High", "Low"), 
         replicate = factor(replicate))

ctmax.model = lme4::lmer(data = filtered_data, 
                         ctmax ~ clade * temp_cent + (1 | site) + (1 | replicate) + (1|tube))

performance::check_model(ctmax.model)

lmerTest::ranova(ctmax.model)
car::Anova(ctmax.model, type = "III")

```

### Acclimation vs. site differences (within- and between-site temperature)

A single temperature slope mixes two processes. Within a site, CTmax changes across the season as the same population experiences warmer or cooler water, which is mostly acclimation. Between sites, CTmax differs with each site's typical temperature, which reflects acclimation plus any local adaptation. Collection temperature was therefore split into a within-site component (collection temperature minus the site's mean collection temperature, so it averages zero at every site) and a between-site component (the site's mean temperature minus the mean across sites) ([van de Pol & Wright 2009](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.anbehav.2008.11.006)). If the between-site slope equals the within-site slope, site differences are explained by acclimation to different temperatures; a steeper between-site slope indicates local adaptation on top of plasticity, and a shallower one countergradient variation. Lineage (X, S, IV and the four F lineages, F-MR, F-FH, F-N and F-NE) is in the model, so turnover of lineages along the coast does not inflate the between-site slope; grouping by clade would not suffice, because the F lineages replace one another between sites (Florida vs. Chesapeake). The assay terms are kept as in the CTmax model above; body size is not included, so the temperature slopes include any effect acting through body size.

The site temperature is the long-term (2014–2023, full-year) MUR SST mean (`Output_data/site_climatology.csv`, Section 1), not the mean of the collection temperatures, which depends on which seasons were sampled (MR and FH only at peak and late). The within-site component stays centred on each site's collection temperatures. Lineage-specific within-site slopes are estimated for lineages with ≥ 15 individuals and seasonal variation in collection temperature, and lineage-specific between-site slopes only for lineages sampled at ≥ 3 sites (X, S, IV); the remaining lineages share a pooled slope.

```{r}
#| label: within-between-model
wb_clim_file <- here("Output", "Output_data", "site_climatology.csv")
wb_events <- filtered_data %>%
  distinct(site, site_code, season, collection_temp) %>%
  group_by(site, site_code) %>%
  summarise(site_mean_collection = mean(collection_temp), .groups = "drop")
if (file.exists(wb_clim_file)) {
  wb_events <- wb_events %>%
    left_join(read_csv(wb_clim_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% select(site_code, site_temp = temp_mean),
              by = "site_code")
  wb_source <- "long-term MUR SST mean"
} else {
  wb_events <- mutate(wb_events, site_temp = site_mean_collection)
  wb_source <- "mean of the site's collection temperatures"
}
wb_data <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(wb_events, by = c("site", "site_code")) %>%
  mutate(t_within = collection_temp - site_mean_collection,
         t_between = site_temp - mean(wb_events$site_temp))

wb_data <- wb_data %>% filter(!is.na(lineage))
lin_order <- c("F-MR", "F-FH", "F-N", "F-NE", "S", "IV", "X")
lin_n <- wb_data %>%
  group_by(lineage) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            sites = n_distinct(site[site %in% names(which(table(site) >= 5))]),
            within_var = any(tapply(t_within, site, function(x) diff(range(x))) > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
est_w <- lin_n$lineage[lin_n$n >= 15 & lin_n$within_var]
est_b <- lin_n$lineage[lin_n$sites >= 3]
wb_data <- wb_data %>%
  mutate(lineage = factor(lineage, levels = intersect(lin_order, unique(lineage))),
         lin_w = factor(if_else(lineage %in% est_w, as.character(lineage), "other")),
         lin_b = factor(if_else(lineage %in% est_b, as.character(lineage), "other")))

# overall slopes (lineage as intercept only) and lineage-specific slopes
wb_add <- lme4::lmer(ctmax ~ lineage + t_within + t_between +
                       (1 | site) + (1 | replicate) + (1 | tube), data = wb_data)
wb_int <- lme4::lmer(ctmax ~ lineage + lin_w:t_within + lin_b:t_between +
                       (1 | site) + (1 | replicate) + (1 | tube), data = wb_data)

b <- lme4::fixef(wb_add); V <- as.matrix(vcov(wb_add))
diff_est <- b[["t_between"]] - b[["t_within"]]
diff_se <- sqrt(V["t_between", "t_between"] + V["t_within", "t_within"] - 2 * V["t_between", "t_within"])
wb_overall <- tibble(
  term = c("Within site (acclimation)", "Between sites", "Between − within"),
  slope = c(b[["t_within"]], b[["t_between"]], diff_est),
  se = c(sqrt(V["t_within", "t_within"]), sqrt(V["t_between", "t_between"]), diff_se)) %>%
  mutate(lo = slope - 1.96 * se, hi = slope + 1.96 * se)

bi <- lme4::fixef(wb_int); Vi <- as.matrix(vcov(wb_int))
wb_clade <- tibble(term = names(bi)) %>%
  filter(str_detect(term, ":t_within$|:t_between$")) %>%
  mutate(lineage = str_remove(str_remove(term, "^lin_[wb]"), ":t_(within|between)$"),
         component = if_else(str_detect(term, "t_within"), "Within site", "Between sites"),
         slope = bi[term], se = sqrt(diag(Vi)[term]),
         lo = slope - 1.96 * se, hi = slope + 1.96 * se) %>%
  left_join(lin_n %>% transmute(lineage = as.character(lineage), sites, n), by = "lineage") %>%
  mutate(sites = if_else(lineage == "other", NA_integer_, sites),
         n = if_else(lineage == "other", NA_integer_, n),
         lineage = if_else(lineage == "other", "other lineages (pooled)", lineage))

knitr::kable(wb_overall, digits = 3,
             caption = paste0("CTmax slopes (°C per °C) for within-site and between-site temperature, all lineages (site temperature: ",
                              wb_source, "). 95% CI = ± 1.96 SE."))
```

```{r}
#| label: within-between-clade-table
wb_clade %>%
  mutate(`Slope (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", slope, lo, hi)) %>%
  select(Lineage = lineage, Component = component, `Slope (95% CI)`, Sites = sites, Individuals = n) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Component, values_from = `Slope (95% CI)`, values_fill = "–") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Lineage-specific CTmax slopes. Sites = sites with ≥ 5 individuals of the lineage. Between-site slopes are estimated only for lineages at ≥ 3 sites and rest on few sites; lineages without their own slope share the pooled slope.")
```

```{r}
#| label: within-between-plot
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 9
plot_lins <- lin_n$lineage[lin_n$n >= 15]
pd <- filter(wb_data, lineage %in% plot_lins) %>% droplevels()
# (A) within site: each site's fitted CTmax across its own collection temperatures
wb_within_lines <- pd %>%
  reframe(t_within = range(t_within),
          .by = c(lineage, lin_w, lin_b, site, site_code, site_mean_collection, t_between)) %>%
  mutate(temp = site_mean_collection + t_within)
wb_within_lines$fit <- predict(wb_int, newdata = wb_within_lines, re.form = ~ (1 | site))

p_within <- ggplot(pd, aes(x = collection_temp, y = ctmax)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = site), alpha = 0.35, size = 1.5) +
  geom_line(data = wb_within_lines, aes(x = temp, y = fit, colour = site, group = site), linewidth = 1.1) +
  facet_wrap(~ lineage, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = site_cols) +
  labs(x = "Collection temperature (°C)", y = "CTmax (°C)", colour = "Site",
       title = "A. Within sites (acclimation)") +
  theme_matt_facets(base_size = 12)

# (B) between sites: each site's CTmax at its own mean collection conditions (no within-site
# deviation; fixed effects + site effect) against the site temperature; line = between-site
# slope, drawn for lineages with their own slope (>= 3 sites)
wb_site_pts <- pd %>%
  group_by(lineage, lin_w, lin_b, site, site_code, site_mean_collection, site_temp, t_between) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 5) %>%
  mutate(t_within = 0)
wb_site_pts$fit <- predict(wb_int, newdata = wb_site_pts, re.form = ~ (1 | site))
wb_between_line <- wb_site_pts %>%
  filter(lineage %in% est_b) %>%
  reframe(t_between = seq(min(t_between), max(t_between), length.out = 20), .by = c(lineage, lin_w, lin_b)) %>%
  mutate(t_within = 0, site_temp = t_between + mean(wb_events$site_temp))
wb_between_line$fit <- predict(wb_int, newdata = wb_between_line, re.form = NA)

p_between <- ggplot(wb_site_pts, aes(x = site_temp, y = fit)) +
  geom_line(data = wb_between_line, colour = "black", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = site), size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ lineage, nrow = 1, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = site_cols) +
  labs(x = paste0("Site temperature (°C; ", wb_source, ")"), y = "Site CTmax (°C)", colour = "Site",
       title = "B. Between sites",
       caption = "Lineages with ≥ 15 individuals. B: each site's fitted CTmax at its mean collection conditions (sites with ≥ 5 individuals);\nline = lineage-specific between-site slope (lineages at ≥ 3 sites).") +
  theme_matt_facets(base_size = 12)

ggarrange(p_within, p_between, ncol = 1, common.legend = TRUE, legend = "right")
```

CTmax rises by `r sprintf("%.2f", wb_overall$slope[1])` °C for every 1 °C of within-site temperature change (95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", wb_overall$lo[1], wb_overall$hi[1])`), with lineage-specific acclimation slopes of `r sprintf("%.2f", min(wb_clade$slope[wb_clade$component == "Within site"]))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(wb_clade$slope[wb_clade$component == "Within site"]))`. The between-site slope is `r sprintf("%.2f", wb_overall$slope[2])` (CI `r sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", wb_overall$lo[2], wb_overall$hi[2])`; site temperature: `r wb_source`), and the difference between the two is `r sprintf("%.2f", wb_overall$slope[3])` (CI `r sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", wb_overall$lo[3], wb_overall$hi[3])`). If that interval includes zero, CTmax differences between sites within a lineage are consistent with acclimation to each site's temperature, with no detectable local adaptation beyond it; with only 1–5 sites per lineage, the test can rule out only large differences between the slopes. Panel B shows the site-level pattern behind the between-site slope: each point is a site's CTmax at its own mean collection conditions.


The Stage 1 clade calls (Section 3.1) were merged with the CTmax and body size data set to examine clade-specific patterns of divergence. By plotting CTmax and size against the collection temperature we can see that these clades appear to be physiologically differentiated. Clades F and S tend to have higher CTmax, even when collected at the same temperatures as Clades X and IV. Size is more variable, with varying degrees of temperature sensitivity across the clades. Overall, however, Clade F tends to be smaller than Clades S and X. Clade IV tended to be the largest.

The general result here is that Clade F appears to be more thermally tolerant than Clades S and X, which in turn are more thermally tolerant than Clade IV. Clade IV does however, appear to exibit stronger plasticity than the other clades (although this pattern is only marginally significant in two of the comparisons; IV-S and IV-X)

These differences in physiology correspond to the distributional patterns for each clade. Using a Loess smoother (span = 2) highlights how the proportional abundance of the clades is affected by temperature in different ways. Clade F occurs in high proportion at high temperature, Clade IV occurs in high proportions at low temperatures, while Clade X occurs in high proportions at intermediate temperatures. Clade S generally occurs in low proportions, with a few exceptions.

### Partitioning CTmax variation

How much of the variation in CTmax among individuals is due to lineage, to the site an animal comes from, to the conditions at collection (acclimation), to the assay, and to individuals? The variance was partitioned with a mixed model with random effects for lineage, site, collection (site × sampling event), assay run and tube position, plus, in the second model, fixed effects for the within- and between-site temperature components from the previous section (body size is not included). The variance explained by each fixed effect is the variance of its fitted contribution ([Nakagawa & Schielzeth 2013](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2041-210x.2012.00261.x)). Comparing the two models shows how much of the site and collection components the temperature terms absorb: collection-level variance taken up by within-site temperature is acclimation, and site-level variance taken up by long-term site temperature is the between-site temperature effect. Intervals are from 200 parametric bootstrap replicates.

```{r}
#| label: ctmax-variance-partition
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5
vp_data <- wb_data %>% mutate(collection = paste(site_code, season, sep = "_"))
vp_m0 <- lme4::lmer(ctmax ~ 1 + (1 | lineage) + (1 | site) + (1 | collection) + (1 | replicate) + (1 | tube),
                    data = vp_data)
vp_m1 <- lme4::lmer(ctmax ~ t_within + t_between + (1 | lineage) + (1 | site) + (1 | collection) +
                      (1 | replicate) + (1 | tube), data = vp_data)

vp_shares <- function(m) {
  vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(m))
  re <- setNames(vc$vcov, vc$grp)
  b <- lme4::fixef(m)
  fx <- c(t_within = NA_real_, t_between = NA_real_)
  if ("t_within" %in% names(b)) fx <- c(t_within = var(b[["t_within"]] * m@frame$t_within),
                                        t_between = var(b[["t_between"]] * m@frame$t_between))
  comp <- c(Lineage = re[["lineage"]], `Site temperature` = unname(fx["t_between"]),
            `Site (other)` = re[["site"]], `Acclimation (within-site temperature)` = unname(fx["t_within"]),
            `Collection (other)` = re[["collection"]],
            Assay = re[["replicate"]] + re[["tube"]], Individual = re[["Residual"]])
  comp[is.na(comp)] <- 0
  comp / sum(comp)
}
set.seed(1)
vp_boot <- function(m) {
  bt <- lme4::bootMer(m, vp_shares, nsim = 200, type = "parametric", use.u = FALSE)
  tibble(component = names(bt$t0), share = bt$t0,
         lo = apply(bt$t, 2, quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE), hi = apply(bt$t, 2, quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))
}
vp_tab <- bind_rows(vp_boot(vp_m0) %>% mutate(model = "Without temperature"),
                    vp_boot(vp_m1) %>% mutate(model = "With within/between temperature")) %>%
  mutate(component = factor(component, levels = names(vp_shares(vp_m1))),
         model = factor(model, levels = c("Without temperature", "With within/between temperature")))

vp_cols <- c(Lineage = "#555555", `Site temperature` = unname(lat_gradient["MR"]), `Site (other)` = "#E8B4A6",
             `Acclimation (within-site temperature)` = unname(lat_gradient["X"]), `Collection (other)` = "#A9BCD9",
             Assay = "#D0D0D0", Individual = "#EDEDED")
ggplot(filter(vp_tab, share > 0), aes(x = model, y = share, fill = component)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, colour = "white") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = vp_cols, name = NULL) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of CTmax variance") +
  theme_matt(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: ctmax-variance-partition-table
vp_tab %>%
  filter(share > 0) %>%
  mutate(value = sprintf("%.0f%% (%.0f–%.0f)", 100 * share, 100 * lo, 100 * hi)) %>%
  select(component, model, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = value, values_fill = "–") %>%
  arrange(component) %>%
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Component", "Without temperature", "With within/between temperature"),
               caption = "Share of CTmax variance (95% parametric bootstrap interval).")
```

```{r}
#| include: false
vc <- function(comp, mod = "With within/between temperature") round(100 * filter(vp_tab, component == comp, model == mod)$share)
```

Without temperature terms, the largest components are collection (`r vc("Collection (other)", "Without temperature")`%), lineage (`r vc("Lineage", "Without temperature")`%) and site (`r vc("Site (other)", "Without temperature")`%), with `r vc("Individual", "Without temperature")`% among individuals within a collection. Adding the temperature terms, within-site temperature (acclimation) explains `r vc("Acclimation (within-site temperature)")`% of all CTmax variance and absorbs most of the collection component (which drops to `r vc("Collection (other)")`%), while long-term site temperature explains `r vc("Site temperature")`% and the remaining site component is `r vc("Site (other)")`%. Lineage accounts for `r vc("Lineage")`%. Thermal tolerance in this complex is therefore structured roughly equally by lineage, by acclimation to recent conditions, and by site (temperature plus other site differences), with little left to the assay. The intervals are wide because lineage and site have few levels (7 lineages, 8 sites).




### Lineage differences under shared conditions (natural common garden)

Lineage accounts for about a quarter of CTmax variance (above), but lineages occupy different sites, so their differences could partly reflect the conditions they were collected in. Several collections, however, contain two or more lineages sampled at the same time and place: those animals experienced the same water before the assay, so differences between them cannot be acclimation. Lineage differences were therefore re-estimated using only collections with ≥ 2 lineages of ≥ 3 individuals each, with collection as a fixed effect, so each lineage contrast is a within-collection comparison. These estimates are compared with the lineage effects from all collections (the within/between model above, which adjusts for temperature but compares lineages across different collections). Differences that persist within collections are heritable (genetic, or developmental/maternal), not plastic responses to recent conditions.

```{r}
#| label: common-garden
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.5
cg_all <- wb_data %>% mutate(collection = paste(site_code, season, sep = "_"))
cg_keep <- cg_all %>%
  count(collection, lineage) %>%
  filter(n >= 3) %>%
  group_by(collection) %>% filter(n() >= 2) %>% ungroup()
cg <- semi_join(cg_all, cg_keep, by = c("collection", "lineage")) %>% droplevels()
cg_model <- lm(ctmax ~ collection + lineage, data = cg)
cg_pairs <- cg_keep %>%
  group_by(collection) %>%
  summarise(pairs = list(combn(sort(as.character(lineage)), 2, paste, collapse = " – ")), .groups = "drop") %>%
  unnest(pairs) %>% count(pairs, name = "collections")
cg_emm <- emmeans::emmeans(cg_model, ~ lineage)
cg_con <- as_tibble(summary(pairs(cg_emm, adjust = "none"), infer = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(pair = str_remove_all(str_replace_all(contrast, " - ", " – "), "[()]")) %>%
  mutate(pair_sorted = map_chr(str_split(pair, " – "), ~ paste(sort(.x), collapse = " – ")),
         sign = if_else(pair == pair_sorted, 1, -1),
         estimate = sign * estimate, lo = if_else(sign == 1, lower.CL, -upper.CL),
         hi = if_else(sign == 1, upper.CL, -lower.CL)) %>%
  inner_join(cg_pairs, by = c("pair_sorted" = "pairs")) %>%
  select(pair = pair_sorted, collections, estimate, lo, hi, p.value)
# the same contrasts from all collections (within/between model: lineage effects at equal temperature)
all_emm <- emmeans::emmeans(wb_add, ~ lineage)
all_con <- as_tibble(summary(pairs(all_emm, adjust = "none"), infer = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(pair = str_remove_all(str_replace_all(contrast, " - ", " – "), "[()]"),
         pair_sorted = map_chr(str_split(pair, " – "), ~ paste(sort(.x), collapse = " – ")),
         sign = if_else(pair == pair_sorted, 1, -1),
         est_all = sign * estimate, lo_all = if_else(sign == 1, lower.CL, -upper.CL),
         hi_all = if_else(sign == 1, upper.CL, -lower.CL)) %>%
  select(pair = pair_sorted, est_all, lo_all, hi_all)
cg_tab <- left_join(cg_con, all_con, by = "pair")

cg_plot <- cg %>%
  mutate(clade = factor(if_else(str_detect(lineage, "^F"), "F", as.character(lineage)), levels = tonsa_clades))
ggplot(cg_plot, aes(x = lineage, y = ctmax, colour = clade)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, alpha = 0.5, size = 1.6) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, colour = "black", size = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ collection, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = clade_cols[tonsa_clades], guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "CTmax (°C)", caption = "Collections with ≥ 2 lineages of ≥ 3 individuals; black = mean ± SE.") +
  theme_matt_facets(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: common-garden-table
cg_tab %>%
  transmute(`Lineage pair (first − second)` = pair, `Shared collections` = collections,
            `Within shared collections` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", estimate, lo, hi),
            p = signif(p.value, 2),
            `All collections (temperature-adjusted)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", est_all, lo_all, hi_all)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "CTmax differences (°C, 95% CI) between lineages that co-occur in at least one collection: estimated only within shared collections, and from all collections in the within/between model.")
```



The two largest lineage differences hold up when lineages are compared side by side. IV is about 2.5–2.9 °C less tolerant than X and S in the same collections (three and one shared collections), as large as or larger than the difference estimated across all collections. F-N is about 0.8 °C more tolerant than S across the three Chesapeake collections where both occur (MD early and late, GW late), close to its overall estimate. These differences cannot be acclimation. The S–X difference is the exception: about 1 °C across all collections, but only 0.4 °C (CI spanning zero) in the two Connecticut collections where they co-occur, so part of it may reflect where each lineage was collected rather than the lineages themselves. The F-MR and F-NE contrasts each rest on a single collection and are uninformative. Caveats: co-occurring lineages may differ in body size, development or recent history (for example, advection from elsewhere), so "heritable" here means not explained by shared recent conditions, not necessarily genetic.


#### Does lineage turnover change seasonal thermal tolerance?

If lineages differ heritably in CTmax and their make-up changes through the season, turnover alone shifts the CTmax a collection would have, independent of acclimation. For each collection, the expected CTmax from composition alone is the composition-weighted mean of the lineage effects (temperature-adjusted lineage means from the within/between model). Its within-site slope against collection temperature (site as a fixed effect, weighted by individuals) is compared with the within-site acclimation slope. The null shuffles lineage labels among individuals across the seasons of each site (10⁴ permutations), keeping each site's lineages but removing their timing.

```{r}
#| label: turnover-ctmax
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
lin_eff <- as_tibble(summary(emmeans::emmeans(wb_add, ~ lineage))) %>%
  transmute(lineage = as.character(lineage), mu = emmean)
comp_t <- comp %>% filter(as.character(lineage) %in% lin_eff$lineage) %>%
  mutate(mu = lin_eff$mu[match(as.character(lineage), lin_eff$lineage)])
coll_exp <- function(d) d %>% group_by(site_code, season) %>%
  summarise(exp_ctmax = mean(mu), temp = mean(collection_temp, na.rm = TRUE), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
turn_slope <- function(ce) {
  ce <- ce %>% group_by(site_code) %>% filter(n() > 1) %>% ungroup()
  unname(coef(lm(exp_ctmax ~ site_code + temp, data = ce, weights = n))["temp"])
}
ce_obs <- coll_exp(comp_t)
slope_obs <- turn_slope(ce_obs)
set.seed(2)
by_site_t <- split(comp_t, comp_t$site_code, drop = TRUE)
slope_null <- replicate(1e4, {
  d <- map_dfr(by_site_t, function(x) { x$mu <- sample(x$mu); x })
  turn_slope(coll_exp(d))
})
slope_p <- (sum(abs(slope_null) >= abs(slope_obs)) + 1) / (length(slope_null) + 1)
acc_slope <- unname(lme4::fixef(wb_add)["t_within"])

ce_obs %>%
  group_by(site_code) %>% filter(n() > 1) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(site_code = factor(site_code, levels = site_order)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = temp, y = exp_ctmax, colour = site_code, group = site_code)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pop_cols[site_order], name = "Site") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 4), name = "Individuals") +
  labs(x = "Collection temperature (°C)", y = "Expected CTmax from lineage composition (°C)") +
  theme_matt(base_size = 13)
```

Composition alone shifts expected CTmax by `r sprintf("%.2f", slope_obs)` °C per °C of collection temperature within sites (permutation p `r if (slope_p < 1e-3) "< 0.001" else paste("=", signif(slope_p, 2))`), compared with an acclimation slope of `r sprintf("%.2f", acc_slope)` °C per °C within lineages: turnover adds about `r round(100 * slope_obs / acc_slope)`% to the seasonal change that acclimation produces. `r if (slope_obs > 0) "Collections are dominated by more tolerant lineages when the water is warm and by less tolerant lineages (above all IV) when it is cool, so turnover reinforces acclimation rather than opposing it." else "Turnover does not move tolerance in the direction of temperature."` This is a seasonal change in thermal tolerance with a heritable basis that happens through the sorting of lineages, not evolution within them. Caveat: composition comes from the individuals sequenced per collection (about 20), so proportions are coarse, and collections were sampled in one year.


### Genetic basis of CTmax within collections

Is CTmax variation among individuals collected together associated with particular genetic variants? Within each lineage with ≥ 30 phenotyped and sequenced individuals (collections with ≥ 8 individuals of the lineage: X 104, F-N 78, S 54, F-FH 38, IV 36), CTmax was regressed on genotype dosage (the expected number of minor alleles, from ANGSD genotype posteriors) at every SNP, with collection and log mean sequencing depth as covariates. Collection absorbs acclimation and population differences, so individuals are compared only with others collected at the same time and place; depth is included because at < 1× coverage deeper individuals show more minor alleles, which would otherwise bias every SNP's effect if depth tracks CTmax (it does, weakly: +0.26 °C per log unit of depth within collections, all lineages pooled). Individuals without reads at a SNP were given their collection's mean dosage. Body size was not included. Genome-wide calibration comes from 100 replicates with CTmax shuffled among individuals of the same collection, which keep each collection's CTmax distribution and all genotype structure but break any genotype–phenotype link.

```{r}
#| label: gwas-qq
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4
gwas_lins <- c("X", "F-N", "S", "F-FH", "IV")
gwas_qq_files <- cx("results", "16_gwas", paste0(gwas_lins, ".qq.tsv"))
if (!all(file.exists(gwas_qq_files))) {
  cat("CTmax association results are not in this export yet.")
} else {
  gwas_qq <- map2_dfr(gwas_lins, gwas_qq_files, function(l, f) {
    read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% mutate(lineage = l)
  }) %>%
    group_by(lineage) %>%
    arrange(desc(bin_lo), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(n_snps = sum(observed),
           Observed = cumsum(observed), `Shuffled CTmax (mean of 100)` = cumsum(perm_mean),
           `Uniform expectation` = n_snps * 10^(-bin_lo)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    pivot_longer(c(Observed, `Shuffled CTmax (mean of 100)`, `Uniform expectation`),
                 names_to = "series", values_to = "count") %>%
    filter(count >= 0.5, bin_lo <= 8) %>%
    mutate(lineage = factor(lineage, levels = gwas_lins))
  ggplot(gwas_qq, aes(x = bin_lo, y = count, colour = series, linetype = series)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    facet_wrap(~ lineage, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_y_log10() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Observed = "black", `Shuffled CTmax (mean of 100)` = unname(lat_gradient["X"]),
                                   `Uniform expectation` = "grey60"), name = NULL) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Observed = "solid", `Shuffled CTmax (mean of 100)` = "solid",
                                     `Uniform expectation` = "dashed"), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = expression(-log[10](p) ~ "threshold"), y = "SNPs with p below threshold") +
    theme_matt_facets(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: gwas-rank-table
gwas_rank_files <- cx("results", "16_gwas", paste0(gwas_lins, ".rank.tsv"))
if (all(file.exists(gwas_rank_files))) {
  gwas_rank <- map2_dfr(gwas_lins, gwas_rank_files, function(l, f) {
    read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% mutate(lineage = l)
  }) %>% filter(snp_set == "all")

      filter(perm == 0, snp_set == "all") %>% transmute(lineage = l, snps)
  })
  gwas_rank %>%
    mutate(value = if_else(statistic == "lambda",
                           sprintf("%.2f vs %.2f (%d)", observed, perm_mean, rank),
                           sprintf("%.0f vs %.0f (%d)", observed, perm_mean, rank))) %>%
    select(lineage, statistic, value) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = statistic, values_from = value) %>%
    left_join(gwas_snps, by = "lineage") %>%
    relocate(snps, .after = lineage) %>%
    mutate(lineage = factor(lineage, levels = gwas_lins)) %>% arrange(lineage) %>%
    knitr::kable(col.names = c("Lineage", "SNPs", "λ", "p < 10⁻³", "p < 10⁻⁴", "p < 10⁻⁵", "p < 10⁻⁶"),
                 caption = "Observed vs. mean of 100 within-collection CTmax shuffles (rank of the observed value among the 101; 1 = larger than every shuffle).")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: gwas-concordance
#| include: false
if (all(file.exists(gwas_rank_files))) {
  # (1) do CTmax effects line up with spatial / seasonal temperature slopes? (unlinked SNPs)
  # (2) do rare minor alleles tend to lower CTmax more than expected from the shuffles?
  read_unl <- function(l) {
    a <- read_tsv(cx("results", "16_gwas", paste0(l, ".assoc.unlinked.tsv.gz")), show_col_types = FALSE,
                  col_types = cols(chrom = "c"))
    pm <- read_tsv(cx("results", "16_gwas", paste0(l, ".perm_t.unlinked.tsv.gz")), show_col_types = FALSE,
                   col_types = cols(chrom = "c"))
    inner_join(a, pm, by = c("chrom", "pos"))
  }
  gwas_conc <- map_dfr(c("X", "S"), function(l) {
    m <- read_unl(l) %>%
      inner_join(read_tsv(cx("results", "14_concordance", paste0(l, ".unlinked.snps.tsv.gz")),
                          show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(chrom = "c")), by = c("chrom", "pos"))
    Tp <- pmin(pmax(as.matrix(select(m, matches("^t[0-9]+$"))), -10), 10)
    t0 <- pmin(pmax(m$t, -10), 10)
    map_dfr(c("z_spatial", "z_seasonal"), function(z) {
      r0 <- cor(t0, m[[z]]); rp <- apply(Tp, 2, cor, m[[z]])
      tibble(comparison = if_else(z == "z_spatial", "Spatial slope", "Seasonal slope"),
             r = r0, perm_sd = sd(rp), rank = sum(abs(rp) >= abs(r0)) + 1)
    }) %>% mutate(lineage = l, snps = nrow(m))
  })
  gwas_sign <- map_dfr(gwas_lins, function(l) {
    m <- read_unl(l) %>% filter(freq < 0.15)
    Tp <- as.matrix(select(m, matches("^t[0-9]+$")))
    neg_frac <- function(t) { s <- abs(t) > 2.6; if (sum(s) == 0) NA_real_ else mean(t[s] < 0) }
    obs <- neg_frac(m$t); pf <- apply(Tp, 2, neg_frac)
    tibble(lineage = l, snps = sum(abs(m$t) > 2.6), observed = obs, perm_mean = mean(pf, na.rm = TRUE),
           lo = quantile(pf, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE), hi = quantile(pf, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
           rank = sum(pf >= obs, na.rm = TRUE) + 1)
  })
}
```

```{r}
#| label: gwas-concordance-table
if (exists("gwas_conc")) {
  gwas_conc %>%
    transmute(Lineage = lineage, Comparison = comparison, `Unlinked SNPs` = snps,
              r = sprintf("%.3f", r), `Shuffle SD of r` = sprintf("%.3f", perm_sd), Rank = paste0(rank, " / 101")) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = "Correlation between each SNP's CTmax effect (t) and its spatial or seasonal temperature slope (z), against 100 within-collection CTmax shuffles (two-sided rank).")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: gwas-sign-table
if (exists("gwas_sign")) {
  gwas_sign %>%
    transmute(Lineage = factor(lineage, levels = gwas_lins), `SNPs (freq < 0.15, |t| > 2.6)` = snps,
              `Observed` = sprintf("%.2f", observed),
              `Shuffles: mean (95% range)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", perm_mean, lo, hi),
              Rank = paste0(rank, " / 101")) %>%
    arrange(Lineage) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = "Fraction of the stronger associations at rare SNPs (minor-allele frequency < 0.15) in which the minor allele lowers CTmax, observed vs. shuffles.")
}
```

No lineage shows more association signal than the shuffles: the observed counts of small p values sit inside, and in X below, the shuffle distribution at every threshold, with or without chromosome 6. The one marginal exception is IV, where moderately small p values (p < 0.001) are more common than in 94 of 100 shuffles but the tail is not; with five lineages tested and the smallest sample (36 individuals, 2 collections), this is consistent with chance. The smallest individual p values (down to ~10⁻⁷–10⁻⁸) are typical of the shuffles too, and the top SNPs share a profile – low frequency, reads in only part of the individuals, large estimated effects – expected from chance at weakly informative sites, so none is reported as a candidate.

Two patterns that appeared in a first version of the scan (without the depth covariate, and with missing individuals given the overall rather than the collection mean) do not survive comparison with the shuffles. First, CTmax effects do not line up with the spatial or seasonal temperature slopes in X or S: the observed correlations (|r| ≤ 0.011) are well inside the shuffle distributions, whose spread (SD 0.01–0.05) is much larger than a chromosome jackknife suggests, because one shuffle shifts the effects of all SNPs together. Second, the excess of negative effects at rare SNPs (minor allele lowering CTmax) is reproduced by the shuffles (63–86% negative in X, S and F-FH, as observed), so it is a property of dosage regression at low-frequency sites, not evidence for deleterious rare variants; only F-N is slightly above its shuffles (0.69 vs. 0.58, rank 4 of 101), which with five lineages tested is not significant.

CTmax among individuals collected together therefore shows no detectable association with individual variants, no polygenic excess, and no link between the alleles that track temperature in space or season and those that affect CTmax. With 36–104 individuals per lineage this rules out only loci of large effect; it is consistent with the variance partition above, in which CTmax variation is dominated by lineage, acclimation and site.



### Candidate genes: mitochondrial amino-acid differences

Lineage differences in CTmax are heritable but, within lineages, no SNP associates with CTmax. The comparative alternative asks which protein differences between lineages could underlie them. Mitochondrial OXPHOS genes are the first candidates: they are inherited as a unit, they define the clades, and amino-acid changes in COX1, CYTB and other respiratory-chain subunits alter thermal performance in copepods (*Tigriopus californicus*: Willett 2010, Harada et al. 2019) and other ectotherms. The clade mitogenome contigs are unannotated de novo assemblies, so protein-coding genes were found as open reading frames (invertebrate mitochondrial code, ≥ 150 codons; COX1 and CYTB identified by conserved motifs, other ORFs by length and strand). ORFs nested inside an ORF on the opposite strand are flagged; one member of each such pair is probably not a gene. The F contig (16.1 kb) covers most of the mitogenome, so the four F lineages can be compared across 11 ORFs; the X and IV contigs (about 5 kb) cover only COX1, CYTB and one further ORF, so clades are compared there (`Scripts/07_mito_aa.R`).

```{r}
#| label: mito-aa
mito_dir <- here("Output", "Output_data", "mito_aa")
have_mito <- file.exists(file.path(mito_dir, "IV_specific_aa.csv"))
if (have_mito) {
  f_orfs <- read_csv(file.path(mito_dir, "F_lineage_orfs.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  f_sites <- read_csv(file.path(mito_dir, "F_lineage_aa_sites.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  cl_pairs <- read_csv(file.path(mito_dir, "clade_aa_pairs.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  iv_aa <- read_csv(file.path(mito_dir, "IV_specific_aa.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  # pairwise F-lineage amino-acid differences (both lineages fixed, >= 80%)
  f_fixed <- f_sites %>% filter(!is.na(state), freq >= 0.8)
  f_lins <- sort(unique(f_sites$lineage))
  f_pairs <- combn(f_lins, 2, simplify = FALSE) %>% map_dfr(\(p) {
    w <- f_fixed %>% filter(lineage %in% p) %>%
      select(gene, aa_pos, lineage, state) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = lineage, values_from = state) %>%
      filter(!is.na(.data[[p[1]]]), !is.na(.data[[p[2]]]))
    tibble(pair = paste(p, collapse = " – "), compared_genes = "all ORFs",
           differences = sum(w[[p[1]]] != w[[p[2]]]),
           differences_excl_ORF216 = sum(w[[p[1]]] != w[[p[2]]] & w$gene != "ORF216-"))
  })
}
```

```{r}
#| label: mito-aa-orfs
if (have_mito) {
  f_orfs %>%
    transmute(ORF = gene, Strand = strand, `Position (bp)` = paste(start, end, sep = "–"), Codons = codons,
              `Nested antisense` = if_else(nested_antisense, "yes", ""),
              `Fixed nt differences` = fixed_nt_differences, Nonsynonymous = nonsynonymous,
              Synonymous = synonymous) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = "Open reading frames on the F mitogenome contig and nucleotide differences fixed (≥ 80% of ≥ 5 called individuals) between at least two F lineages.")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: mito-aa-fpairs
if (have_mito) {
  f_pairs %>% select(-compared_genes) %>%
    rename(`Lineage pair` = pair, `Amino-acid differences` = differences,
           `Excluding ORF216-` = differences_excl_ORF216) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = "Fixed amino-acid differences between F lineages, all ORFs on the F contig.")
}
```

```{r}

if (have_mito) {
  cl_pairs %>%
    mutate(value = sprintf("%d / %d", differences, aligned_aa)) %>%
    mutate(pair = str_replace(pair, "-", " – ")) %>%
    select(gene, pair, value) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = gene, values_from = value) %>%
    rename(`Clade pair` = pair, `ORF (LQDA)` = ORF_LQDA) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = "Amino-acid differences between clade consensus proteins (differences / aligned positions) in the three genes covered by all four clade contigs.")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: mito-aa-iv
if (have_mito) {
  iv_aa %>%
    rename(Gene = gene, `Position (F protein)` = pos_F, `F, S, X` = F_S_X, `Context (F)` = context_F) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = "Substitutions unique to IV, the low-CTmax clade (IV differs; F, S and X share the state).")
}
```

`r if (have_mito) paste0("COX1 is almost invariant: ", sum(f_orfs$nonsynonymous[f_orfs$gene == "COX1"]), " nonsynonymous against ", sum(f_orfs$synonymous[f_orfs$gene == "COX1"]), " synonymous fixed differences among F lineages, and at most ", max(cl_pairs$differences[cl_pairs$gene == "COX1"]), " amino-acid differences between any two clades. CYTB and the other ORFs carry most of the amino-acid divergence. ", nrow(iv_aa), " substitutions are unique to IV (", paste(sprintf("%d in %s", as.vector(table(iv_aa$gene)), names(table(iv_aa$gene))), collapse = ", "), ").") else ""`

These are candidates, not results. Every substitution on the branch leading to IV is equally consistent with IV's low CTmax, and with one low-CTmax clade there is no replication to separate causal changes from the many neutral ones that accumulated with them. Two observations constrain the mitochondrial explanation. First, among F lineages, the southern F-MR differs from F-N at about 90 amino acids, yet with S as a common yardstick (both co-occur with S) F-MR is not more tolerant than F-N: F-MR exceeds S by 0.3 °C at MR, and F-N exceeds S by 0.8 °C in the Chesapeake. Large mitochondrial divergence within F does not translate into a CTmax difference. Second, IV is not more divergent than other clades in COX1, the most constrained OXPHOS gene. The useful next step is structural: placing the IV-specific CYTB and COX1 substitutions on the respiratory-complex structures (quinone-binding sites of complex III, the proton channels of complex IV) to see whether any sit where function, rather than sequence, changes. ORF216- is unreliable: it has no calls in F-FH or F-MR, and F-N and F-NE differ there mostly at nonsynonymous sites, the pattern of a misassembled or non-coding region rather than a gene.

The nuclear part of the candidate analysis (heat-shock proteins, nuclear OXPHOS subunits, lipid desaturases and elongases) needs the RefSeq annotation of the reference genome (GCF_053477335.1), which is not yet in the project.


### Trait variability within clades

Shown below is the trait variation (ranges) for each site. Ranges are calculated for each collection separately.

```{r}
#| label: trait-range-plot
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.5
trait_ranges = join_data %>% 
  drop_na(clade) %>% 
  filter(clade != "A_hudsonica") %>% 
  group_by(site, season, clade, collection_temp, collection_salinity, doy, lat) %>% 
  summarise(mean_ctmax = mean(ctmax),
            ctmax_range = max(ctmax) - min(ctmax),
            ctmax_var = var(ctmax),
            mean_size = mean(size),
            size_range = max(size) - min(size),
            size_var = var(size)) %>% 
  mutate(prop_ctmax_range = ctmax_range / mean_ctmax,
         prop_size_range = size_range / mean_size)

ctmax_range_temp = ggplot(trait_ranges, aes(x = collection_temp, y = ctmax_range)) + 
  facet_wrap(clade~.) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "black", se = F) + 
  geom_point(aes(colour = site), 
             size = 3) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = site_cols) + 
  labs(y = "CTmax Range (°C)",
       x = "Collection Temp. (°C)") +
  theme_matt() + 
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ctmax_var_temp = ggplot(trait_ranges, aes(x = collection_temp, y = ctmax_var, colour = site)) + 
  facet_wrap(clade~.) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "black", se = F) + 
  geom_point(aes(colour = site), 
             size = 3) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = site_cols) + 
  labs(y = "CTmax Variance",
       x = "Collection Temp. (°C)") +
  theme_matt() + 
  theme(legend.position = "right")

size_range_temp = ggplot(trait_ranges, aes(x = collection_temp, y = size_range, colour = site)) + 
  facet_wrap(clade~.) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "black", se = F) + 
  geom_point(aes(colour = site), 
             size = 3) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = site_cols) + 
  labs(y = "Size Range (mm)",
       x = "Collection Temp. (°C)") +
  theme_matt() + 
  theme(legend.position = "right")

size_var_temp = ggplot(trait_ranges, aes(x = collection_temp, y = size_var, colour = site)) + 
  facet_wrap(clade~.) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "black", se = F) + 
  geom_point(aes(colour = site), 
             size = 3) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = site_cols) + 
  labs(y = "Size Variance",
       x = "Collection Temp. (°C)") +
  theme_matt() + 
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggarrange(ctmax_var_temp, size_var_temp, common.legend = T, legend = "right")
```

Changes in trait variance may be indicative of phenotypic selection. If selection (as opposed to acclimation) are driving seasonal changes, we may expect to see a reduction in variance in the peak samples relative to the early season samples. Note that early season collection temperatures this year were higher than expected, driven by fairly strong heatwaves across the North Atlantic. As shown in the temperature profiles for each site, the 'early' samples were collected just after high temperatures were reached, while 'peak' samples were collected after sites had experienced high temperatures for several weeks (generations). As warming tolerances were fairly high throughout this period, we will assume that selection was weak before the early samples. If the early onset of high temperatures filtered out vulnerable genotypes prior to our sampling, the results will be a conservative estimate of the effects of selection on trait variance.

### Parasites, epibionts and thermal limits

Infected and uninfected individuals are compared within the same collection (same site, date and collection temperature), so differences are not confounded with acclimation temperature. Only collections with at least two positive and two negative individuals are shown.

```{r}
#| label: infection-traits
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 7
inf_groups <- c(paradinium = "Paradinium", trematode = "Trematodes",
                apostome = "Apostome ciliates", peritrich = "Peritrich ciliates")
inf <- join_data %>%
  select(sample_id, site_code, season, clade, ctmax, size, paste0(names(inf_groups), "_call")) %>%
  pivot_longer(ends_with("_call"), names_to = "group", values_to = "positive",
               names_pattern = "(.*)_call") %>%
  mutate(collection = paste(site_code, season)) %>%
  group_by(group, collection) %>%
  filter(sum(positive) >= 2, sum(!positive) >= 2) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(group = factor(inf_groups[group], levels = inf_groups),
         status = factor(if_else(positive, "positive", "negative"), levels = c("negative", "positive")))

if (nrow(inf) == 0) {
  cat("No collection has both infected and uninfected individuals.")
} else {
  inf %>%
    pivot_longer(c(ctmax, size), names_to = "trait") %>%
    mutate(trait = recode(trait, ctmax = "CTmax (°C)", size = "Prosome length (mm)")) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = collection, y = value, colour = status)) +
    facet_grid(trait ~ group, scales = "free", space = "free_x",
               labeller = labeller(group = label_wrap_gen(12))) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.6),
               size = 1.8, alpha = 0.8) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 95, size = 10,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(negative = "grey65", positive = "grey10")) +
    labs(x = "Collection (site, season)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
    theme_matt_facets(base_size = 13) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: infection-models
infection_fit <- function(var) {
  d <- join_data %>%
    mutate(collection = paste(site_code, season), status = .data[[var]]) %>%
    group_by(collection) %>% filter(any(status), any(!status)) %>% ungroup()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(NULL)
  map_dfr(c("ctmax", "size"), function(tr) {
    m <- lme4::lmer(as.formula(paste(tr, "~ status + clade + (1 | collection)")), data = d)
    co <- summary(m)$coefficients["statusTRUE", ]
    tibble(covariate = var, trait = tr, n_collections = n_distinct(d$collection),
           n_positive = sum(d$status), effect = co[["Estimate"]], se = co[["Std. Error"]])
  })
}
bind_rows(infection_fit("parasite_any"), infection_fit("epibiont_any")) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3,
               caption = "Effect of carrying a parasite or epibiont on CTmax and size, within collections (trait ~ status + clade + (1 | collection)); only collections with both positive and negative individuals.")
```

## 5. Partitioning vulnerability

Warming tolerance (CTmax minus habitat temperature) is the usual summary of vulnerability, and it is usually computed from a single CTmax per species. The results above show that "*A. tonsa*" CTmax varies at two levels that a single value ignores: heritable differences between lineages (common garden), and acclimation within lineages, which is the same across sites and seasons (within/between model). Lineage make-up also changes through the season. Three scenarios show how much each level changes where the species looks vulnerable.

- **Fixed CTmax:** one value for everyone, the mean of all peak-season individuals.
- **Lineage means:** each lineage's peak-season mean CTmax (its mean over all collections when it has < 5 peak-season individuals), weighted by the lineage make-up of the site's peak collection.
- **Lineages + acclimation:** CTmax predicted for each lineage on each day from the within/between model (population-level, no site random effect): lineage + within-site temperature (the day's temperature minus the site's mean collection temperature) + between-site temperature (the site's long-term MUR mean). The day's temperature is clamped to the range of collection temperatures at which that lineage was sampled, so acclimation is not extrapolated beyond the data. Same peak-season make-up.

Habitat temperature is the bias-corrected daily MUR SST, 2014–2023 (Section 1), plus 0 or 4 °C for a uniform-warming scenario. Two summaries per site, over August–September (the warmest months, peak abundance, and the period the peak collections represent): the mean warming tolerance of the peak-season population, and the warming tolerance on the warmest August–September day of each year (averaged over years) for the least tolerant lineage making up ≥ 10% of the peak collection. Intervals are 95% ranges from 1,000 bootstrap resamples of individuals (fixed and lineage means) or 1,000 draws of the model's fixed effects (lineages + acclimation). Individuals' CTmax was measured against collection-day water temperature, while predictions use MUR SST, which in summer runs cooler than the in-situ collection temperatures at the northern sites (Section 1); the acclimation scenario therefore uses MUR temperatures on a model fitted to in-situ ones.

```{r}
#| label: wt-scenarios
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6.5
mur_file <- here("Output", "Output_data", "mur_sst_daily_corrected.csv")
have_mur <- file.exists(mur_file)
if (!have_mur) cat("MUR daily temperatures (Output_data/mur_sst_daily_corrected.csv) are not available.")
```

```{r}
#| label: wt-scenarios-compute
#| include: false
if (have_mur) {
  B <- 1000
  set.seed(5)
  scen_levels <- c("Fixed CTmax", "Lineage means", "Lineages + acclimation")
  wt_lin <- levels(wb_data$lineage)
  peak_days <- read_csv(mur_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(site_code %in% site_order, month(date) %in% 8:9) %>%
    transmute(site_code, year = year(date), temp = sst_c)
  comp_peak <- comp %>% filter(season == "peak") %>%
    count(site_code, lineage) %>% group_by(site_code) %>% mutate(p = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(site_code = as.character(site_code), lineage = as.character(lineage))
  comp_annual <- comp %>%
    count(site_code, lineage) %>% group_by(site_code) %>% mutate(p = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(site_code = as.character(site_code), lineage = as.character(lineage))
  lin_trange <- wb_data %>% group_by(lineage = as.character(lineage)) %>%
    summarise(tmin = min(collection_temp), tmax = max(collection_temp), .groups = "drop")
  site_terms <- wb_events %>%
    transmute(site_code, smc = site_mean_collection, tb = site_temp - mean(wb_events$site_temp))

  # temperature aggregates per site x lineage: Aug-Sep mean, and warmest day per year (mean over years)
  temp_agg <- function(dw, compo) {
    d <- peak_days %>% mutate(temp = temp + dw)
    hot <- d %>% group_by(site_code, year) %>% slice_max(temp, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()
    compo %>%
      inner_join(lin_trange, by = "lineage") %>%
      inner_join(site_terms, by = "site_code") %>%
      rowwise() %>%
      mutate(mT = mean(d$temp[d$site_code == site_code]),
             mTc = mean(pmin(pmax(d$temp[d$site_code == site_code], tmin), tmax)),
             hT = mean(hot$temp[hot$site_code == site_code]),
             hTc = mean(pmin(pmax(hot$temp[hot$site_code == site_code], tmin), tmax))) %>%
      ungroup()
  }

  # CTmax draws per lineage: column 1 = point estimate, then B draws
  peak_ind <- wb_data %>% filter(season == "peak")
  boot_mean <- function(x) c(mean(x), replicate(B, mean(sample(x, replace = TRUE))))
  ct_fixed <- boot_mean(peak_ind$ctmax)
  ct_lin <- map(set_names(wt_lin), function(l) {
    x <- peak_ind$ctmax[peak_ind$lineage == l]
    if (length(x) < 5) x <- wb_data$ctmax[wb_data$lineage == l]
    boot_mean(x)
  })
  fe <- lme4::fixef(wb_add)
  beta <- rbind(fe, MASS::mvrnorm(B, fe, as.matrix(vcov(wb_add))))
  lin_int <- function(l) beta[, "(Intercept)"] + if (paste0("lineage", l) %in% colnames(beta)) beta[, paste0("lineage", l)] else 0

  # warming tolerance draws for one site: mean (composition-weighted) and warmest-day (least tolerant common lineage)
  site_wt <- function(a, scenario) {
    wt <- map(seq_len(nrow(a)), function(i) {
      r <- a[i, ]
      ct_m <- switch(scenario,
        "Fixed CTmax" = ct_fixed, "Lineage means" = ct_lin[[r$lineage]],
        "Lineages + acclimation" = lin_int(r$lineage) + beta[, "t_within"] * (r$mTc - r$smc) + beta[, "t_between"] * r$tb)
      ct_h <- if (scenario == "Lineages + acclimation")
        lin_int(r$lineage) + beta[, "t_within"] * (r$hTc - r$smc) + beta[, "t_between"] * r$tb else ct_m
      list(mean = ct_m - r$mT, hot = ct_h - r$hT)
    })
    common <- a$p >= 0.10
    list(mean = Reduce(`+`, map2(wt, a$p, ~ .x$mean * .y)),
         hot = do.call(pmin, map(wt[common], "hot")))
  }
  summ <- function(v) tibble(est = v[1], lo = quantile(v[-1], 0.025), hi = quantile(v[-1], 0.975))

  wt_res <- map_dfr(c(0, 4), function(dw) {
    map_dfr(c(scen_levels, "Lineages + acclimation (annual make-up)"), function(sc) {
      compo <- if (grepl("annual", sc)) comp_annual else comp_peak
      ag <- temp_agg(dw, compo)
      map_dfr(split(ag, ag$site_code), function(a) {
        w <- site_wt(a, sub(" \\(annual make-up\\)", "", sc))
        bind_rows(mutate(summ(w$mean), metric = "Aug–Sep mean"),
                  mutate(summ(w$hot), metric = "Warmest day, least tolerant common lineage")) %>%
          mutate(site_code = a$site_code[1])
      }) %>% mutate(scenario = sc, warming = dw)
    })
  }) %>%
    mutate(site_code = factor(site_code, levels = site_order))
  write_csv(wt_res, here("Output", "Output_data", "wt_scenarios.csv"))

  # spread among sites, current conditions, with bootstrap intervals for the change vs fixed CTmax
  wt_range <- wt_res %>% filter(warming == 0) %>%
    group_by(scenario, metric) %>%
    summarise(range = max(est) - min(est), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(metric) %>%
    mutate(change = 100 * (range / range[scenario == "Fixed CTmax"] - 1)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = c(scen_levels, "Lineages + acclimation (annual make-up)"))) %>%
    arrange(metric, scenario)
  write_csv(wt_range %>% transmute(Scenario = scenario, Metric = metric, `WT range among sites` = range,
                                   `Change vs fixed (%)` = change),
            here("Output", "Output_data", "wt_range_changes.csv"))
}
```

}

  wt_sites_low <- wt_res %>% filter(warming == 4, metric == "Warmest day, least tolerant common lineage") %>%

`r if (have_mur) { r <- filter(wt_range, metric == "Aug–Sep mean"); h <- filter(wt_range, metric != "Aug–Sep mean"); sprintf("Relative to a single CTmax, lineage means change the spread of peak-season warming tolerance among sites by %+.0f%%, and lineages with acclimation by %+.0f%% (warmest-day metric: %+.0f%% and %+.0f%%). With +4 °C, the lowest warming tolerance on the warmest day is at %s.", r$change[r$scenario == 'Lineage means'], r$change[r$scenario == 'Lineages + acclimation'], h$change[h$scenario == 'Lineage means'], h$change[h$scenario == 'Lineages + acclimation'], paste(sprintf('%s under %s (%.1f °C)', wt_sites_low$site_code, wt_sites_low$scenario, wt_sites_low$est), collapse = '; ')) } else ""`

What changes, site by site:

- **A single CTmax makes the south look more vulnerable and the north less vulnerable than its lineages are.** Florida's lineages (F-FH, F-MR) are the most tolerant, so lineage means raise Florida's warming tolerance by about 3 °C, enough that +4 °C warming no longer pushes the warmest day to zero. The northern sites' X and IV are less tolerant than the species average, so their margin drops by about 2 °C. Peak-season means in the Chesapeake and Connecticut barely move, because their peak-season lineages (F-N, S) are close to the average; at CT the warmest-day margin still drops by 2 °C, set by the X minority.
- **Acclimation adds little at the peak and helps most under warming.** The peak-season means already include acclimation to summer water, so acclimation changes current warming tolerance by a few tenths of a degree; with +4 °C it adds up to about 2 °C (GW), limited by the clamp to sampled temperatures. Its intervals are the widest, because it rests on a model rather than direct measurements.
- **Seasonal turnover keeps the least tolerant lineage out of the heat.** Using each site's make-up over all collections instead of the peak collection lowers the warmest-day margin by about 2 °C at CT and TK, because IV, the least tolerant lineage, is common there only in autumn. Annual composition would overstate vulnerability where turnover is strongest.

These are illustrations, not forecasts: they assume composition and the acclimation response stay as observed, warming is uniform through the season, and CTmax is the relevant limit.
